title.zh: 卷502 列傳二百八十九 艺術一
title.raw: 卷502 列傳二百八十九 艺術一

sentences.zh: 葉桂薛雪吳瑭章楠王士雄徐大椿王維德吳謙

translations.literal: Ye Gui, Xue Xue, Wu Tang, Zhang Nan, Wang Shixiong, Xu Dachun, Wang Weide, Wu Qian
translations.idiomatic: Ye Gui, Xue Xue, Wu Tang, Zhang Nan, Wang Shixiong, Xu Dachun, Wang Weide, and Wu Qian.

sentences.zh: 綽爾濟伊桑阿張朝魁陸懋修王丙呂震鄒澍費伯雄

translations.literal: Chuoerji, Yisang'a, Zhang Chaokui, Lu Maoxiu, Wang Bing, Lü Zhen, Zou Shu, Fei Boxiong
translations.idiomatic: Chuoerji, Yisang'a, Zhang Chaokui, Lu Maoxiu, Wang Bing, Lü Zhen, Zou Shu, and Fei Boxiong.

sentences.zh: 蔣平階章攀桂劉祿張永祚戴尚文=【序】=自司馬遷傳扁鵲、倉公及日者、龜策，史家因之，或曰方技，或曰藝術。

translations.literal: Jiang Pingjie, Zhang Pangui, Liu Lu, Zhang Yongzuo, Dai Shangwen. [Preface] Since Sima Qian wrote biographies of Bian Que, Cang Gong, and the specialists in day-selection and tortoise-shell divination, historians have followed his example, calling such figures either fangji (technical specialists) or yishu (arts).
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Pingjie, Zhang Pangui, Liu Lu, Zhang Yongzuo, and Dai Shangwen. [Preface] Ever since Sima Qian wrote biographies of Bian Que, Cang Gong, and the day-selection and tortoise-shell diviners, later historians have followed his lead, grouping such figures under the headings of "technical specialists" or "the arts."

sentences.zh: 大抵所收多醫、卜、陰陽、術數之流，間及工巧。

translations.literal: For the most part what they record are physicians, diviners, yin-yang masters, and practitioners of numerology, with occasional mention of craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: For the most part they record physicians, diviners, masters of yin-yang lore, and practitioners of numerology, with craftsmen mentioned only now and then.

sentences.zh: 夫藝之所賅，博矣眾矣，古以禮、樂、射、禦、書、數為六藝，士所常肄，而百工所執，皆藝事也。

translations.literal: The scope of the arts is vast and manifold: in antiquity ritual, music, archery, charioteering, writing, and arithmetic were the Six Arts that scholars regularly studied, while everything the hundred crafts practiced was also an art.
translations.idiomatic: The scope of the arts is vast and manifold. In antiquity ritual, music, archery, charioteering, writing, and arithmetic formed the Six Arts that scholars regularly studied, while everything the hundred crafts practiced counted as an art as well.

sentences.zh: 近代方志，於書畫、技擊、工巧併入此類，實有合於古義。

translations.literal: In modern local gazetteers, painting and calligraphy, martial arts, and craftsmanship are all placed in this category, which truly accords with the ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Modern local gazetteers place painting and calligraphy, martial arts, and craftsmanship in this same category, which truly accords with the ancient meaning.

sentences.zh: 聖祖天縱神明，多能藝事，貫通中、西曆算之學，一時鴻碩，蔚成專家，國史躋之儒林之列。

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor was heaven-endowed with divine intelligence and mastered many arts; he thoroughly penetrated Chinese and Western calendrical and mathematical learning, and the great scholars of the age who became specialists in these fields were ranked in the dynastic histories among the Confucian literati.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven-endowed with divine intelligence, the Kangxi Emperor mastered many arts and thoroughly penetrated Chinese and Western calendrical and mathematical learning. The great scholars of his age who became specialists in these fields were ranked in the dynastic histories among the Confucian literati.

sentences.zh: 測繪地圖，鑄造槍砲，始仿西法。

translations.literal: Surveying and mapping, casting guns and cannon—all at first followed Western methods.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying and mapping, and casting guns and cannon—all at first followed Western methods.

sentences.zh: 凡有一技之能者，往往召直蒙養齋。

translations.literal: Whenever someone possessed even a single skill, he was often summoned to serve in the Mengyangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever someone possessed even a single skill, he was often summoned to serve in the Mengyangzhai (Hall for the Nurture of Youth).

sentences.zh: 其文學侍從之臣，每以書畫供奉內廷。

translations.literal: Literary attendants were often ordered to present paintings and calligraphy for service within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: His literary attendants were often ordered to present paintings and calligraphy for service within the palace.

sentences.zh: 又設如意館，制仿前代畫院，兼及百工之事。

translations.literal: The Ruyiguan was also established, modeled on the painting academies of earlier dynasties and including work in the hundred crafts.
translations.idiomatic: The Ruyiguan (Hall of As-You-Will) was also established, modeled on the painting academies of earlier dynasties and including work in the hundred crafts.

sentences.zh: 故其時供禦器物，雕、組、陶埴，靡不精美，傳播寰瀛，稱為極盛。

translations.literal: Thus objects made for the imperial court—carving, embroidery, pottery—were all exquisite; spread throughout the world, they were called the height of splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Thus objects made for the imperial court—whether carving, embroidery, or pottery—were all exquisite. Spread throughout the world, they were acclaimed as the height of splendor.

sentences.zh: 沿及高宗之世，風不替焉。

translations.literal: This continued into the Qianlong reign without decline.
translations.idiomatic: This continued into the Qianlong reign without decline.

sentences.zh: 欽定醫宗金鑑，薈萃古今學說，宗旨純正。

translations.literal: The Imperial Medical Golden Mirror was compiled by imperial order, gathering ancient and modern medical doctrines with a pure and correct aim.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order the Yizong Jinjian (Golden Mirror of the Medical Tradition) was compiled, gathering ancient and modern medical doctrines with a pure and correct aim.

sentences.zh: 於陰陽術數家言，亦有協紀辨方一書，頒行沿用，從俗從宜，隱示崇實黜虛之意，斯徵微尚矣。

translations.literal: For the yin-yang and numerology schools there was also the Xieji Bianfang, issued for use according to custom and convenience, implicitly showing a preference for the real and rejection of the empty—a subtle sign indeed.
translations.idiomatic: For the yin-yang and numerology schools there was also the Xieji Bianfang, issued for use according to custom and convenience, implicitly showing a preference for the real and rejection of the empty—a subtle sign indeed.

sentences.zh: 中葉後，海禁大開，泰西藝學諸書，灌輸中國，議者以工業為強國根本，於是研格致，營製造者，乘時而起。

translations.literal: After the mid-dynasty the maritime prohibitions were greatly relaxed; books on Western arts poured into China, and advocates held industry to be the foundation of a strong state, so those who studied natural philosophy and undertook manufacture rose with the times.
translations.idiomatic: After the mid-dynasty the maritime prohibitions were greatly relaxed. Books on Western arts poured into China, and advocates held industry to be the foundation of a strong state, so those who studied natural philosophy and undertook manufacture rose with the times.

sentences.zh: 或由舊學以擴新知，或抒心得以濟實用，世乃愈以藝事為重。

translations.literal: Some expanded new knowledge from old learning; some expressed insight to serve practical use—the age came increasingly to value the arts.
translations.idiomatic: Some expanded new knowledge from old learning; some expressed insight to serve practical use—and the age came increasingly to value the arts.

sentences.zh: 採其可傳者著於篇，各以類為先後。

translations.literal: Those worth transmitting are set down in these chapters, each class arranged in order.
translations.idiomatic: Those worth transmitting are set down in these chapters, each class arranged in order.

sentences.zh: 卓然成家者，具述授受源流；

translations.literal: Those who established schools in their own right are fully described with their lines of transmission;
translations.idiomatic: Those who established schools in their own right are fully described with their lines of transmission;

sentences.zh: 兼有政績、文學列入他傳者，附存梗概；

translations.literal: those whose political achievements or literary accomplishments are recorded in other biographies have summaries appended;
translations.idiomatic: those whose political achievements or literary accomplishments appear in other biographies have summaries appended;

sentences.zh: 凡涉荒誕俳諧之說，屏勿載。

translations.literal: every tale involving the absurd or the comic is excluded.
translations.idiomatic: every tale involving the absurd or the comic is excluded.

sentences.zh: 後之覽者，庶為論世之資雲。

translations.literal: Readers hereafter may thus have material for judging the age.
translations.idiomatic: Readers hereafter may thus have material for judging the age.

sentences.zh: 吳有性，字又可，江南吳縣人。

translations.literal: Wu Youxing, courtesy name Youke, a native of Wu County in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youxing, courtesy name Youke, was a native of Wu County in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 生於明季，居太湖中洞庭山。

translations.literal: Born in the late Ming, he lived on Dongting Mountain in Lake Tai.
translations.idiomatic: Born in the late Ming, he lived on Dongting Mountain in Lake Tai.

sentences.zh: 當崇禎辛巳歲，南北直隸、山東、浙江大疫，醫以傷寒法治之，不效。

translations.literal: In the xinsi year of the Chongzhen reign, great epidemics struck Zhili, Shandong, and Zhejiang north and south; physicians treated them by cold-damage methods without effect.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year of the Chongzhen reign, great epidemics struck Zhili, Shandong, and Zhejiang north and south. Physicians treated them with cold-damage methods without effect.

sentences.zh: 有性推究病源，就所歷驗，著瘟疫論，謂：「傷寒自毫竅入，中於脈絡，從表入裡，故其傳經有六。

translations.literal: Youxing investigated the source of the disease and, from his own experience, wrote On Pestilence, saying: "Cold damage enters through the pores and strikes the channels and collaterals, passing from the exterior to the interior; hence its transmission through the channels has six stages.
translations.idiomatic: Youxing investigated the source of the disease and, drawing on his own experience, wrote On Pestilence, saying: "Cold damage enters through the pores and strikes the channels and collaterals, passing from the exterior to the interior; hence its transmission through the channels has six stages.

sentences.zh: 自陽至陰。

translations.literal: From yang to yin.
translations.idiomatic: From yang to yin.

sentences.zh: 以次而深。

translations.literal: Each stage deeper than the last.
translations.idiomatic: Each stage deeper than the last.

sentences.zh: 瘟疫自口鼻入，伏於膜原，其邪在不表不里之間。

translations.literal: Pestilence enters through the mouth and nose and lies hidden in the membrane source; its evil lies between neither exterior nor interior.
translations.idiomatic: Pestilence enters through the mouth and nose and lies hidden in the membrane source; its evil lies between neither exterior nor interior.

sentences.zh: 其傳變有九，或表或裡，各自為病。

translations.literal: Its transformations have nine forms, sometimes exterior and sometimes interior, each becoming a disease in its own right.
translations.idiomatic: Its transformations have nine forms, sometimes exterior and sometimes interior, each becoming a disease in its own right.

sentences.zh: 有但表而不裡者，有表而再表者，有但里而不表者，有里而再裡者，有表里分傳者，有表里分傳而再分傳者，有表勝於裡者，有先表後裡者，有先里後表者。」

translations.literal: There are cases only in the exterior without the interior, cases exterior and then exterior again, only interior without exterior, interior and then interior again, exterior and interior transmitting separately, exterior and interior transmitting separately and then separating again, exterior prevailing over interior, exterior first and interior later, and interior first and exterior later."
translations.idiomatic: There are cases only in the exterior without the interior, cases that are exterior and then exterior again, only interior without exterior, interior and then interior again, exterior and interior transmitting separately, exterior and interior transmitting separately and then separating again, exterior prevailing over interior, exterior first and interior later, and interior first and exterior later."

sentences.zh: 其間有與傷寒相反十一事，又有變證、兼證，種種不同。

translations.literal: Among these there are eleven points opposite to cold damage, and also variant and combined patterns, each different.
translations.idiomatic: Among these there are eleven points opposite to cold damage, and also variant and combined patterns, each different.

sentences.zh: 並著論制方，一一辨別。

translations.literal: He also wrote treatises and prescriptions, distinguishing each one.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote treatises and prescriptions, distinguishing each one.

sentences.zh: 古無瘟疫專書，自有性書出，始有發明。

translations.literal: In antiquity there was no specialized book on pestilence; only after Youxing's book appeared was there real discovery.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity there was no specialized book on pestilence; only after Youxing's book appeared was there real discovery.

sentences.zh: 其後有戴天章、余霖、劉奎，皆以治瘟疫名。

translations.literal: After him came Dai Tianzhang, Yu Lin, and Liu Kui, all famed for treating pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: After him came Dai Tianzhang, Yu Lin, and Liu Kui, all famed for treating pestilence.

sentences.zh: 天章，字麟郊，江蘇上元人。

translations.literal: Tianzhang, courtesy name Linjiao, a native of Shangyuan in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Tianzhang, courtesy name Linjiao, was a native of Shangyuan in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 好學強記，尤精於醫。

translations.literal: Fond of learning and with a strong memory, he was especially skilled in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of learning and with a strong memory, he was especially skilled in medicine.

sentences.zh: 所著傷寒、雜病諸書，及咳論注、瘧論注、廣瘟疫論，凡十餘種。

translations.literal: His works on cold damage and miscellaneous diseases, and his commentaries on cough and malaria, and his Expanded Treatise on Pestilence, totaled more than ten kinds.
translations.idiomatic: His works on cold damage and miscellaneous diseases, his commentaries on cough and malaria, and his Expanded Treatise on Pestilence totaled more than ten kinds.

sentences.zh: 其論瘟疫，一宗有性之說。

translations.literal: In discussing pestilence he wholly followed Youxing's doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: In discussing pestilence he wholly followed Youxing's doctrine.

sentences.zh: 謂瘟疫之異於傷寒，尤慎辨於見證之始。

translations.literal: He said that what distinguishes pestilence from cold damage must be carefully discerned at the very first manifestation.
translations.idiomatic: He said that what distinguishes pestilence from cold damage must be carefully discerned at the very first manifestation.

sentences.zh: 辨氣、辨色、辨舌、辨神、辨脈，益加詳焉。

translations.literal: Discerning qi, color, tongue, spirit, and pulse—he added still greater detail.
translations.idiomatic: Discerning qi, color, tongue, spirit, and pulse—he added still greater detail.

sentences.zh: 為人療病，不受謝。

translations.literal: In treating others he accepted no reward.
translations.idiomatic: In treating others he accepted no reward.

sentences.zh: 子瀚，成雍正元年一甲第二名進士。

translations.literal: His son Han became jinshi in the first rank, second place, in the first year of the Yongzheng reign.
translations.idiomatic: His son Han placed second in the first rank of the palace examination in the first year of the Yongzheng reign.

sentences.zh: 霖，字師愚，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Lin, courtesy name Shiyu, a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, courtesy name Shiyu, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，桐城疫，霖謂病由熱淫，投以石膏，輒愈。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign Tongcheng suffered an epidemic; Lin said the disease came from heat excess and prescribed gypsum, which always cured.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong reign Tongcheng suffered an epidemic. Lin said the disease came from heat excess and prescribed gypsum, which always cured.

sentences.zh: 後數年，至京師，大暑，疫作，醫以張介賓法者多死，以有性法亦不盡驗。

translations.literal: Several years later he went to the capital; in great heat an epidemic broke out. Physicians using Zhang Jiebin's methods mostly died; those using Youxing's method did not always succeed either.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later he went to the capital. In great heat an epidemic broke out. Physicians using Zhang Jiebin's methods mostly died; those using Youxing's method did not always succeed either.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚卿馮應榴姬人呼吸將絕，霖與大劑石膏，應手而痊，踵其法​​者，活人無算。

translations.literal: The concubine of Grand Secretary Feng Yingli was near death, her breath failing; Lin gave a large dose of gypsum and she recovered at once. Those who followed his method saved countless lives.
translations.idiomatic: The concubine of Grand Secretary Feng Yingli was near death, her breath failing. Lin gave a large dose of gypsum and she recovered at once. Those who followed his method saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 霖所著曰疫疹一得，其論與有性有異同，取其辨證，而以用達原飲及三消、承氣諸方，猶有附會表里之意云。

translations.literal: Lin's work is called Unique Insights on Epidemic Rashes; its theory differs in places from Youxing's, taking its pattern differentiation while use of Dayuan Decoction and the Three Eliminations and Chengqi formulas still bears something of exterior-interior doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's work is called Unique Insights on Epidemic Rashes. Its theory differs in places from Youxing's, taking its pattern differentiation while use of Dayuan Decoction and the Three Eliminations and Chengqi formulas still bears something of exterior-interior doctrine.

sentences.zh: 奎，字文甫，山東諸城人。

translations.literal: Kui, courtesy name Wenfu, a native of Zhucheng in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, courtesy name Wenfu, was a native of Zhucheng in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 乾隆末，著瘟疫論類編及松峰說疫二書，松峰者，奎以自號也。

translations.literal: At the end of the Qianlong reign he wrote Classified Treatise on Pestilence and Songfeng on Epidemics; Songfeng was Kui's sobriquet.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qianlong reign he wrote Classified Treatise on Pestilence and Songfeng on Epidemics; Songfeng was Kui's sobriquet.

sentences.zh: 多為窮鄉僻壤艱覓醫藥者說法。

translations.literal: He chiefly explained methods for remote villages that could hardly obtain medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He chiefly explained methods for remote villages that could hardly obtain medicine.

sentences.zh: 有性論瘟疫，已有大頭瘟、疙瘩瘟疫、絞腸瘟、軟腳瘟之稱，奎复舉北方俗諺所謂諸疫證名狀，一一剖析之。

translations.literal: Youxing had already named big-head pestilence, lump pestilence, twisted-intestine pestilence, and soft-foot pestilence; Kui further listed epidemic patterns from northern popular sayings and analyzed each.
translations.idiomatic: Youxing had already named big-head pestilence, lump pestilence, twisted-intestine pestilence, and soft-foot pestilence. Kui further listed epidemic patterns from northern popular sayings and analyzed each.

sentences.zh: 又以貧寒病家無力購藥，取鄉僻恆有之物可療病者，發明其功用，補本草所未備，多有心得。

translations.literal: He also, for poor families unable to buy medicine, took things commonly found in the countryside that could treat disease and explained their uses, supplementing what the materia medica had not recorded, with many insights.
translations.idiomatic: He also, for poor families unable to buy medicine, took things commonly found in the countryside that could treat disease and explained their uses, supplementing what the materia medica had not recorded, with many insights.

sentences.zh: 同時昌邑黃元禦治疫，以浮萍代麻黃，即本奎說。

translations.literal: At the same time Huang Yuanyu of Changyi treated epidemics using duckweed in place of ephedra, following Kui's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Huang Yuanyu of Changyi treated epidemics using duckweed in place of ephedra, following Kui's teaching.

sentences.zh: 所著書流傳日本，醫家著述，亦有取焉。

translations.literal: His books circulated in Japan, and medical writers there also drew on them.
translations.idiomatic: His books circulated in Japan, and medical writers there also drew on them.

sentences.zh: 喻昌，字嘉言，江西新建人。

translations.literal: Yu Chang, courtesy name Jiayan, a native of Xinjian in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Chang, courtesy name Jiayan, was a native of Xinjian in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 幼能文，不羈，與陳際泰遊。

translations.literal: As a youth he could write; unrestrained, he associated with Chen Jitai.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he could write. Unrestrained, he associated with Chen Jitai.

sentences.zh: 明崇禎中，以副榜貢生入都上書言事，尋詔徵，不就，往來靖安間。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, as a sub-list graduate he went to the capital and submitted a memorial on state affairs; he was soon summoned but did not take office, traveling between Jing'an and elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chongzhen reign of the Ming, as a sub-list graduate he went to the capital and submitted a memorial on state affairs. He was soon summoned but did not take office, traveling between Jing'an and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 披為僧，复蓄髮游江南。

translations.literal: He was tonsured as a monk, then let his hair grow again and traveled in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: He was tonsured as a monk, then let his hair grow again and traveled in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治中，僑居常熟，以醫名，治療多奇中。

translations.literal: In the Shunzhi reign he lived in Changshu and became famed as a physician; his cures were often miraculously effective.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shunzhi reign he lived in Changshu and became famed as a physician; his cures were often miraculously effective.

sentences.zh: 才辯縱橫，不可一世。

translations.literal: His talent and eloquence were unbounded; he considered no one his equal.
translations.idiomatic: His talent and eloquence were unbounded; he considered no one his equal.

sentences.zh: 著傷寒尚論篇，謂林億、成無已過於尊信王叔和，惟方有執作條辨，削去叔和序例，得尊經之旨；

translations.literal: He wrote Discourses on Cold Damage, saying Lin Yi and Cheng Wuyi overly revered Wang Shuhe; only Fang Youzhi's Detailed Differentiation, removing Shuhe's preface and arrangement, grasped the meaning of honoring the classics;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Discourses on Cold Damage, saying Lin Yi and Cheng Wuyi overly revered Wang Shuhe; only Fang Youzhi's Detailed Differentiation, removing Shuhe's preface and arrangement, grasped the meaning of honoring the classics;

sentences.zh: 而猶有未達者，重為編訂，其淵源雖出方氏，要多自抒所見。

translations.literal: yet there were still points not reached; he re-edited the work. Though its source lay in Fang, it mostly expressed his own views.
translations.idiomatic: yet there were still points not reached, and he re-edited the work. Though its source lay in Fang, it mostly expressed his own views.

sentences.zh: 惟溫證論中，以溫藥治溫病，後尤怡、陸鋰修並著論非之。

translations.literal: Only in his Warm Pattern Treatise he used warm drugs to treat warm disease; later You Yi and Lu Maoxiu both wrote treatises criticizing this.
translations.idiomatic: Only in his Warm Pattern Treatise he used warm drugs to treat warm disease; later You Yi and Lu Maoxiu both wrote treatises criticizing this.

sentences.zh: 又著醫門法律，取風、寒、暑、濕、燥、火六氣及諸雜證，分門著論。

translations.literal: He also wrote Medical Laws, taking wind, cold, summer heat, damp, dry, and fire—the six qi—and miscellaneous patterns, dividing them into treatises.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Medical Laws, taking wind, cold, summer heat, damp, dry, and fire—the six qi—and miscellaneous patterns, dividing them into treatises.

sentences.zh: 次法，次律。

translations.literal: Next methods, next laws.
translations.idiomatic: Next came methods, next laws.

sentences.zh: 法者，治療之術，運用之機；

translations.literal: Methods are the techniques of treatment and the mechanism of application;
translations.idiomatic: Methods are the techniques of treatment and the mechanism of application;

sentences.zh: 律者，明著醫之所以失，而判定其罪，如折獄然。

translations.literal: laws clearly set forth how physicians err and judge their guilt, as in deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: laws clearly set forth how physicians err and judge their guilt, as in deciding cases.

sentences.zh: 昌此書，專為庸醫誤人而作，分別疑似，使臨診者不敢輕嘗，有功醫術。

translations.literal: Chang wrote this book specifically because mediocre physicians harm people; distinguishing what merely resembles a pattern, he made those at the bedside dare not lightly try remedies—service to medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Chang wrote this book specifically because mediocre physicians harm people. By distinguishing what merely resembles a pattern, he made those at the bedside dare not lightly try remedies—a real service to medicine.

sentences.zh: 後附寓意草，皆其所治醫案。

translations.literal: Appended is the Draft of Intent, all his medical cases.
translations.idiomatic: Appended is the Draft of Intent, containing all his medical cases.

sentences.zh: 凡診病，先議病，後用藥，又與門人定議病之式，至詳審。

translations.literal: In every diagnosis he first deliberated on the disease, then used medicine; with his disciples he also fixed the form for deliberating on disease, to the utmost detail.
translations.idiomatic: In every diagnosis he first deliberated on the disease, then used medicine. With his disciples he also fixed the form for deliberating on disease, to the utmost detail.

sentences.zh: 所載治驗，反覆推論，務闡審證用藥之所以然，異於諸家醫案但泛言某病用某藥癒者，並為世所取法。

translations.literal: The cures recorded reason back and forth, always explaining why careful pattern identification and use of medicine were as they were—unlike other medical case collections that only vaguely say a certain disease was cured with a certain drug—and this too became a model for the age.
translations.idiomatic: The cures recorded reason back and forth, always explaining why careful pattern identification and use of medicine were as they were—unlike other medical case collections that only vaguely say a certain disease was cured with a certain drug—and this too became a model for the age.

sentences.zh: 昌通禪理，其醫往往出於妙悟。

translations.literal: Chang understood Chan doctrine; his medicine often arose from subtle insight.
translations.idiomatic: Chang understood Chan doctrine; his medicine often arose from subtle insight.

sentences.zh: 尚論後篇及醫門法律，年七十後始成。

translations.literal: The latter part of his Discourses and Medical Laws were completed only after he was seventy.
translations.idiomatic: The latter part of his Discourses and Medical Laws were completed only after he was seventy.

sentences.zh: 昌既久居江南，從學者甚多。

translations.literal: Chang had long lived in Jiangnan and had many students.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had long lived in Jiangnan and had many students.

sentences.zh: 徐彬，字忠可，浙江嘉興人。

translations.literal: Xu Bin, courtesy name Zhongke, a native of Jiaxing in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bin, courtesy name Zhongke, was a native of Jiaxing in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 昌之弟子。

translations.literal: A disciple of Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He was a disciple of Chang.

sentences.zh: 著傷寒一百十三方發明及金匱要略論注，其說皆本於昌。

translations.literal: He wrote Explication of the One Hundred Thirteen Formulas of Cold Damage and Commentary on the Essentials of the Golden Coffer; his doctrines all derive from Chang.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Explication of the One Hundred Thirteen Formulas of Cold Damage and Commentary on the Essentials of the Golden Coffer; his doctrines all derive from Chang.

sentences.zh: 四庫著錄金匱要略，即用彬論注本。

translations.literal: The Siku Catalog's Essentials of the Golden Coffer uses Bin's commentary edition.
translations.idiomatic: The Siku Catalog's Essentials of the Golden Coffer uses Bin's commentary edition.

sentences.zh: 凡疏釋正義，見於注；

translations.literal: Correct interpretations appear in the commentary;
translations.idiomatic: Correct interpretations appear in the commentary;

sentences.zh: 或賸義及總括諸證不可專屬者，見於論。

translations.literal: remaining meanings and summaries of patterns that cannot belong to a single section appear in the discourses.
translations.idiomatic: remaining meanings and summaries of patterns that cannot belong to a single section appear in the discourses.

sentences.zh: 彬謂：「他方書出於湊集，就採一條，時亦獲驗。

translations.literal: Bin said: "Other formularies are patchwork compilations; take one entry and it may sometimes work.
translations.idiomatic: Bin said: "Other formularies are patchwork compilations; take one entry and it may sometimes work.

sentences.zh: 若金匱之妙，統觀一卷，全體方具。

translations.literal: The wonder of the Golden Coffer is that viewing the whole scroll at once, the complete body is present.
translations.idiomatic: The wonder of the Golden Coffer is that viewing the whole scroll at once, the complete body is present.

sentences.zh: 不獨察其所用，並須察其所不用。」

translations.literal: One must observe not only what is used but also what is not used."
translations.idiomatic: One must observe not only what is used but also what is not used."

sentences.zh: 世以為篤論。

translations.literal: The age regarded this as sound doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The age regarded this as sound doctrine.

sentences.zh: 張璐，字路玉，自號石頑老人，江南長洲人。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu, courtesy name Luyu, sobriquet the Stubborn Old Man of Stone, a native of Changzhou in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu, courtesy name Luyu, sobriquet the Stubborn Old Man of Stone, was a native of Changzhou in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少穎悟，博貫儒業，專心醫藥之書。

translations.literal: In youth clever, he broadly mastered Confucian learning and devoted himself to medical books.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was clever. He broadly mastered Confucian learning and devoted himself to medical books.

sentences.zh: 自軒、岐迄近代方法，無不搜覽。

translations.literal: From the Yellow Emperor and Qi Bo down to methods of recent times, he left nothing unsearched.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow Emperor and Qi Bo down to methods of recent times, he left nothing unsearched.

sentences.zh: 遭明季之亂，隱於洞庭山中十餘年，著書自娛，至老不倦。

translations.literal: Suffering the chaos of the late Ming, he hid on Dongting Mountain for more than ten years, writing for pleasure until old age without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Suffering the chaos of the late Ming, he hid on Dongting Mountain for more than ten years, writing for pleasure until old age without weariness.

sentences.zh: 仿明王肯堂證治準繩，匯集古人方論、近代名言，薈萃折衷之，每門附以治驗醫案，為醫歸一書，後易名醫通。

translations.literal: Following Wang Kentang's Standards of Pattern and Treatment, he gathered ancient formulas and modern sayings, collected and reconciled them, appending medical cases to each section in Medical Return, later renamed Comprehensive Medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Following Wang Kentang's Standards of Pattern and Treatment, he gathered ancient formulas and modern sayings, collected and reconciled them, appending medical cases to each section in Medical Return, later renamed Comprehensive Medicine.

sentences.zh: 璐謂仲景書衍釋日多，仲景之意轉晦。

translations.literal: Lu said that as commentaries on Zhongjing's books grew daily, Zhongjing's meaning grew obscure.
translations.idiomatic: Lu said that as commentaries on Zhongjing's books grew daily, Zhongjing's meaning grew obscure.

sentences.zh: 後見尚論、條辨諸編，又廣蒐秘本，反覆詳玩，始覺向之所謂多歧者，漸歸一貫，著傷寒纘論、緒論。

translations.literal: Later he saw the Discourses, Detailed Differentiation, and other works, widely sought secret editions, studied them repeatedly, and felt what had seemed many divergences gradually became one thread; he wrote Continued and Thread Discourses on Cold Damage.
translations.idiomatic: Later he saw the Discourses, Detailed Differentiation, and other works, widely sought secret editions, studied them repeatedly, and felt what had seemed many divergences gradually became one thread. He wrote Continued and Thread Discourses on Cold Damage.

sentences.zh: 纘者，祖仲景之文；

translations.literal: Continued means following Zhongjing's text;
translations.idiomatic: "Continued" means following Zhongjing's text;

sentences.zh: 緒者，理諸家之紛紜而清出之，以翼仲景之法。

translations.literal: Thread means sorting out the confusion of various schools and clarifying it to support Zhongjing's method.
translations.idiomatic: "Thread" means sorting out the confusion of various schools and clarifying it to support Zhongjing's method.

sentences.zh: 其註本草，疏本經之大義，並系諸家治法，曰本經逢原；

translations.literal: In commenting on the materia medica he clarified the great meaning of the root classic and attached the treatment methods of various schools, calling it Meeting the Root Classic;
translations.idiomatic: In commenting on the materia medica he clarified the great meaning of the root classic and attached the treatment methods of various schools, calling it Meeting the Root Classic;

sentences.zh: 論脈法大義，曰診宗三昧：皆有心得。

translations.literal: on the great meaning of pulse methods he wrote The Threefold Essence of Diagnosis: both had real insight.
translations.idiomatic: on the great meaning of pulse methods he wrote The Threefold Essence of Diagnosis—both had real insight.

sentences.zh: 又謂唐孫思邈治病多有奇異，逐方研求藥性，詳為疏證，曰千金方釋義，並行於世。

translations.literal: He also said Sun Simiao of the Tang often had strange cures; he studied each formula's drug properties in detail and wrote Commentary on the Thousand Gold Formulas, all circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Sun Simiao of the Tang often had strange cures. He studied each formula's drug properties in detail and wrote Commentary on the Thousand Gold Formulas, all circulating in the world.

sentences.zh: 璐著書主博通，持論平實，不立新異。

translations.literal: Lu's books chiefly aim at broad mastery; his arguments are level and solid, establishing no new oddities.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's books chiefly aim at broad mastery; his arguments are level and solid, establishing no new oddities.

sentences.zh: 其治病，則取法薛已、張介賓為多。

translations.literal: In treating disease he chiefly took Xue Ji and Zhang Jiebin as models.
translations.idiomatic: In treating disease he chiefly took Xue Ji and Zhang Jiebin as models.

sentences.zh: 年八十餘卒。

translations.literal: He died in his eighties.
translations.idiomatic: He died at over eighty years of age.

sentences.zh: 聖祖南巡，璐子以柔進呈遺書，溫旨留覽焉。

translations.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor toured the south, Lu's son Yourou presented his father's posthumous books; an imperial warm edict ordered them kept for perusal.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor toured the south, Lu's son Yourou presented his father's posthumous writings. An imperial warm edict ordered them kept for perusal.

sentences.zh: 子登、倬，皆世其業。

translations.literal: His sons Deng and Zhuo both inherited the profession.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Deng and Zhuo both carried on the family profession.

sentences.zh: 登，字誕先，著傷寒舌鑑；

translations.literal: Deng, courtesy name Xianxian, wrote Mirror of the Tongue in Cold Damage;
translations.idiomatic: Deng, courtesy name Xianxian, wrote Mirror of the Tongue in Cold Damage;

sentences.zh: 倬，字飛疇，著傷寒兼證析義：並著錄四庫。

translations.literal: Zhuo, courtesy name Feichou, wrote Analysis of Combined Patterns in Cold Damage: both are recorded in the Siku Catalog.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo, courtesy name Feichou, wrote Analysis of Combined Patterns in Cold Damage—both are recorded in the Siku Catalog.

sentences.zh: 高斗魁，字旦中，又號鼓峰，浙江鄞縣人。

translations.literal: Gao Doukui, courtesy name Danzhong, also called Gufeng, a native of Yin County in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Doukui, courtesy name Danzhong, also called Gufeng, was a native of Yin County in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 兄鬥樞，明季死國難。

translations.literal: His elder brother Doushu died for the state in the late Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Doushu died for the state in the late Ming turmoil.

sentences.zh: 斗魁任俠，於遺民罹難者，破產營救。

translations.literal: Doukui was chivalrous; for loyalist sufferers in hardship he ruined his estate to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Doukui was chivalrous. For loyalist sufferers in hardship he ruined his estate to rescue them.

sentences.zh: 妻因事連及，勒自裁。

translations.literal: His wife was implicated in a case and forced to take her own life.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was implicated in a case and forced to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 素精醫，遊杭，見舁棺者血瀝地，曰：「是未死！」

translations.literal: Skilled in medicine from youth, traveling in Hangzhou he saw bearers of a coffin with blood dripping to the ground and said: "This person is not dead!"
translations.idiomatic: Skilled in medicine from youth, while traveling in Hangzhou he saw bearers of a coffin with blood dripping to the ground and cried: "This person is not dead!"

sentences.zh: 啟棺，與藥而甦。

translations.literal: He opened the coffin, gave medicine, and the man revived.
translations.idiomatic: He opened the coffin, gave medicine, and the man revived.

sentences.zh: 江湖間傳其事，求治病者無寧晷。

translations.literal: The story spread through the rivers and lakes; those seeking treatment gave him no moment's rest.
translations.idiomatic: The story spread through the rivers and lakes, and those seeking treatment gave him no moment's rest.

sentences.zh: 著醫學心法；

translations.literal: He wrote Essentials of Medical Learning;
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essentials of Medical Learning;

sentences.zh: 又吹毛編，則自記醫案也。

translations.literal: and also Blowing Hair, which records his own medical cases.
translations.idiomatic: and also Blowing Hair, which records his own medical cases.

sentences.zh: 其論醫宗旨，亦近於張介賓。

translations.literal: The aim of his medical doctrine was also close to Zhang Jiebin's.
translations.idiomatic: The aim of his medical doctrine was also close to Zhang Jiebin's.

sentences.zh: 周學海，字澂之，安徽建德人，總督馥子。

translations.literal: Zhou Xuehai, courtesy name Chengzhi, a native of Jiande in Anhui, son of Governor Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xuehai, courtesy name Chengzhi, was a native of Jiande in Anhui and son of Governor Fu.

sentences.zh: 光緒十八年進士，授內閣中書，官至浙江候補道。

translations.literal: He became jinshi in the eighteenth year of the Guangxu reign, was appointed Secretariat draftsman, and rose to expectant circuit intendant of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He became jinshi in the eighteenth year of the Guangxu reign, was appointed Secretariat draftsman, and rose to expectant circuit intendant of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 潛心醫學，論脈尤詳，著脈義簡摩、脈簡補義、診家直訣、辨脈平脈章句。

translations.literal: Devoted to medicine, he was especially detailed on the pulse, writing Brief Rubbing of Pulse Meaning, Supplement to Brief Pulse, Straight Formula for Pulse Examiners, and Chapter and Sentence on Discerning and Balancing the Pulse.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to medicine, he was especially detailed on the pulse, writing Brief Rubbing of Pulse Meaning, Supplement to Brief Pulse, Straight Formula for Pulse Examiners, and Chapter and Sentence on Discerning and Balancing the Pulse.

sentences.zh: 引申舊說，參以實驗，多心得之言。

translations.literal: He extended old doctrines and joined them to experiment, with many insights of his own.
translations.idiomatic: He extended old doctrines and joined them to experiment, offering many insights of his own.

sentences.zh: 博覽群籍，實事求是，不取依託附會。

translations.literal: Broadly reading all books, he sought truth from facts and did not rely on forced analogy.
translations.idiomatic: He read broadly and sought truth from facts, refusing forced analogy.

sentences.zh: 慕宋人之善悟，故於史堪、張元素、劉完素、滑壽及近世葉桂諸家書，皆有評註。

translations.literal: Admiring the Song masters' gift for insight, he commented on the books of Shi Kan, Zhang Yuansu, Liu Wansu, Hua Shou, and the near contemporary Ye Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Admiring the Song masters' gift for insight, he commented on the books of Shi Kan, Zhang Yuansu, Liu Wansu, Hua Shou, and the near contemporary Ye Gui.

sentences.zh: 自言於清一代名醫，服膺張璐、葉桂兩家。

translations.literal: He said of famous physicians of the Qing, he most revered Zhang Lu and Ye Gui.
translations.idiomatic: He said that among famous physicians of the Qing he most revered Zhang Lu and Ye Gui.

sentences.zh: 證治每取璐說，蓋其學頗與相近。

translations.literal: In pattern treatment he often took Lu's doctrine, for their learning was quite close.
translations.idiomatic: In pattern treatment he often took Lu's doctrine, for their learning was quite close.

sentences.zh: 宦游江、淮間，時為人療治，常病不異人，遇疑難，輒有奇效。

translations.literal: While serving in office between the Yangtze and Huai, he sometimes treated people; ordinary cases were no different from others, but when he met difficulty he often had remarkable effect.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in office between the Yangtze and Huai, he sometimes treated people. Ordinary cases were no different from others, but when he met difficulty he often achieved remarkable cures.

sentences.zh: 刻古醫書十二種，所據多宋、元舊槧藏家秘笈，校勘精審，世稱善本雲。

translations.literal: He printed twelve kinds of ancient medical books, mostly from Song and Yuan old blocks and collectors' secret editions, with careful collation; the age called them fine editions.
translations.idiomatic: He printed twelve kinds of ancient medical books, mostly from Song and Yuan old blocks and collectors' secret editions, with careful collation—the age called them fine editions.

sentences.zh: 張志聰，字隱庵，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhicong, courtesy name Yin'an, a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhicong, courtesy name Yin'an, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 明末，杭州盧之頤、繇父子著書，講明醫學，志聰繼之。

translations.literal: In the late Ming, Lu Zhiyi and his son You of Hangzhou wrote books clarifying medicine; Zhicong succeeded them.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Ming, Lu Zhiyi and his son You of Hangzhou wrote books clarifying medicine, and Zhicong succeeded them.

sentences.zh: 構侶山堂，招同志講論其中，參考經論，辨其是非。

translations.literal: He built the Lushan Hall and gathered like-minded men to discuss within it, consulting the classics and distinguishing right from wrong.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Lushan Hall and gathered like-minded men to discuss within it, consulting the classics and distinguishing right from wrong.

sentences.zh: 自順治中至康熙之初，四十年間，談軒、岐之學者咸歸之。

translations.literal: From the Shunzhi reign to the early Kangxi, for forty years those who spoke of Xuan and Qi learning all turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: From the Shunzhi reign to the early Kangxi, for forty years those who spoke of Xuan and Qi learning all turned to him.

sentences.zh: 注素問、靈樞二經，集諸家之說，隨文衍義，勝明馬元臺本。

translations.literal: He commented on the Suwen and Lingshu, gathering various schools' sayings and explaining the text as he went, surpassing the Ming edition of Ma Yuantai.
translations.idiomatic: He commented on the Suwen and Lingshu, gathering various schools' sayings and explaining the text as he went, surpassing the Ming edition of Ma Yuantai.

sentences.zh: 又注傷寒論、金匱要略，於傷寒論致力尤深，歷二十年，再易稿始成。

translations.literal: He also commented on Cold Damage and the Essentials of the Golden Coffer; on Cold Damage he labored especially, taking twenty years and revising the draft twice before completion.
translations.idiomatic: He also commented on Cold Damage and the Essentials of the Golden Coffer. On Cold Damage he labored especially, taking twenty years and revising the draft twice before completion.

sentences.zh: 用王叔和原本，略改其編次。

translations.literal: He used Wang Shuhe's original text, slightly altering its arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: He used Wang Shuhe's original text, slightly altering its arrangement.

sentences.zh: 首列六經病，次列霍亂易复並濕、暍汗、吐下，後列辨脈、平脈，而刪叔和序例，以其與本論矛盾，故去之以息辨。

translations.literal: First he listed the six-channel diseases, then cholera, relapse, and damp, summer heat, sweat, vomiting and purging, then discerning and balancing the pulse, and deleted Shuhe's preface and arrangement because they contradicted the main treatise, removing them to quiet dispute.
translations.idiomatic: First he listed the six-channel diseases, then cholera, relapse, and patterns of damp, summer heat, sweat, vomiting and purging, then discerning and balancing the pulse. He deleted Shuhe's preface and arrangement because they contradicted the main treatise, removing them to quiet dispute.

sentences.zh: 駁辨成無已舊注，謂：「風傷衛，寒傷營，脈緩為中風，脈緊為傷寒。

translations.literal: Refuting Cheng Wuyi's old commentary, he said: "Wind injures the defensive, cold injures the constructive; a moderate pulse is wind stroke, a tight pulse is cold damage.
translations.idiomatic: Refuting Cheng Wuyi's old commentary, he said: "Wind injures the defensive, cold injures the constructive; a moderate pulse is wind stroke, a tight pulse is cold damage.

sentences.zh: 傷寒，惡寒無汗，宜麻黃湯；

translations.literal: Cold damage, aversion to cold without sweat, Ephedra Decoction is appropriate;
translations.idiomatic: Cold damage, with aversion to cold and no sweat, Ephedra Decoction is appropriate;

sentences.zh: 中風，惡風有汗，宜桂枝湯：諸說未盡當。

translations.literal: wind stroke, aversion to wind with sweat, Cinnamon Twig Decoction is appropriate: these sayings are not fully correct.
translations.idiomatic: wind stroke, with aversion to wind and sweat, Cinnamon Twig Decoction is appropriate—these sayings are not fully correct.

sentences.zh: 而風、寒兩感，營、衛俱傷，宜大青龍湯為尤謬。

translations.literal: When wind and cold are both felt and constructive and defensive are both injured, Major Blue Dragon Decoction is especially absurd.
translations.idiomatic: When wind and cold are both felt and constructive and defensive are both injured, Major Blue Dragon Decoction is especially absurd.

sentences.zh: 其註，分章以明大旨，節解句釋，兼晰陰陽血氣之生始出入，經脈藏府之貫通循行，使讀論者取之有本，用之無窮，不徒求之糟粕，庶免終身由之而不知其道也。」

translations.literal: His commentary divides chapters to clarify the main idea, explains line by line, and clarifies the birth, movement, and passage of yin-yang and blood-qi and the penetration and circulation of channels and viscera, so readers of the treatise may take it with root and use it without limit, not merely seeking dregs, and may avoid following it all one's life without knowing its Way."
translations.idiomatic: His commentary divides chapters to clarify the main idea, explains line by line, and clarifies the birth, movement, and passage of yin-yang and blood-qi and the penetration and circulation of channels and viscera, so readers may take the treatise with root and use it without limit—not merely seeking dregs—and may avoid following it all one's life without knowing its Way."

sentences.zh: 又注本草，詮釋本經，闡明藥性，本五運六氣之理。

translations.literal: He also commented on the materia medica, interpreting the root classic and clarifying drug nature on the principles of the five movements and six qi.
translations.idiomatic: He also commented on the materia medica, interpreting the root classic and clarifying drug nature on the principles of the five movements and six qi.

sentences.zh: 後人不經臆說，概置勿錄。

translations.literal: Later people's groundless sayings without study were generally set aside and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Later people's groundless sayings without study were generally set aside and not recorded.

sentences.zh: 其自著曰侶山堂類辨、針灸秘傳。

translations.literal: His own works are Classified Discussions of Lushan Hall and Secret Transmission of Acupuncture and Moxibustion.
translations.idiomatic: His own works are Classified Discussions of Lushan Hall and Secret Transmission of Acupuncture and Moxibustion.

sentences.zh: 志聰之學，以素、靈、金匱為歸，生平著書，必守經法，遺書並行於世，惟針灸祕傳佚。

translations.literal: Zhicong's learning took Suwen, Lingshu, and the Golden Coffer as its return; all his life's books kept to the classics. His posthumous books all circulated; only Secret Transmission of Acupuncture is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicong's learning took Suwen, Lingshu, and the Golden Coffer as its goal. All his life's books kept to the classics. His posthumous books all circulated; only Secret Transmission of Acupuncture is lost.

sentences.zh: 高世栻，字士宗。

translations.literal: Gao Shizong, courtesy name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Shizong, courtesy name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 與志聰同里。

translations.literal: Of the same district as Zhicong.
translations.idiomatic: He was of the same district as Zhicong.

sentences.zh: 少家貧，讀時醫通俗諸書，年二十三即出療病，頗有稱。

translations.literal: Poor in youth, he read popular books of contemporary physicians; at twenty-three he went out to treat disease and won some reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Poor in youth, he read popular books of contemporary physicians. At twenty-three he went out to treat disease and won some reputation.

sentences.zh: 後自病，時醫治之，益劇；

translations.literal: Later he fell ill himself; contemporary physicians treated him and he grew worse;
translations.idiomatic: Later he fell ill himself. Contemporary physicians treated him and he grew worse;

sentences.zh: 久之，不藥，幸愈。

translations.literal: after long time, without medicine, he fortunately recovered.
translations.idiomatic: after a long time, without medicine, he fortunately recovered.

sentences.zh: 翻然悔曰：「我治人，殆亦如是，是草菅人命也。」

translations.literal: He repented and said: "When I treat others, it is probably also like this—this is treating human life as grass."
translations.idiomatic: He repented and said: "When I treat others, it is probably also like this—this is treating human life as grass."

sentences.zh: 乃從志聰講論軒、岐、仲景之學，歷十年，悉窺精奧。

translations.literal: Then he studied with Zhicong the learning of Xuan, Qi, and Zhongjing, and in ten years fully penetrated its subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: Then he studied with Zhicong the learning of Xuan, Qi, and Zhongjing, and in ten years fully penetrated its subtlety.

sentences.zh: 遇病必究其本末，處方不同流俗。

translations.literal: When he met disease he always traced root and branch; his prescriptions differed from vulgar fashion.
translations.idiomatic: When he met disease he always traced root and branch, and his prescriptions differed from vulgar fashion.

sentences.zh: 志聰著本草崇原，未竟，世栻繼成之。

translations.literal: Zhicong wrote Honoring the Root of the Materia Medica but did not finish; Shizong completed it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhicong wrote Honoring the Root of the Materia Medica but did not finish; Shizong completed it.

sentences.zh: 又注傷寒論。

translations.literal: He also commented on Cold Damage.
translations.idiomatic: He also commented on Cold Damage.

sentences.zh: 晚著醫學真傳，示門弟子。

translations.literal: In old age he wrote True Transmission of Medicine, showing his disciples.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he wrote True Transmission of Medicine for his disciples.

sentences.zh: 自述曰：「醫理如剝蕉，剝至無可剝，方為至理。

translations.literal: He said of himself: "Medical principle is like stripping a plantain; strip until nothing remains to strip, and that is the ultimate principle.
translations.idiomatic: He said of himself: "Medical principle is like stripping a plantain; strip until nothing remains to strip, and that is the ultimate principle.

sentences.zh: 以之論病，大中至正，一定不移。

translations.literal: Use it to discuss disease and it is centrally correct and unchanging.
translations.idiomatic: Use it to discuss disease and it is centrally correct and unchanging.

sentences.zh: 世行分門別類之方書，皆醫門糟粕，如薛已、趙獻可輩，雖有穎悟變通，非軒、岐、仲景一脈相傳之大道。

translations.literal: Formularies in circulation that divide by category are all dregs of the medical gate; men like Xue Ji and Zhao Xianke, though clever and adaptable, do not transmit the great Way handed down from Xuan, Qi, and Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Formularies in circulation that divide by category are all dregs of the medical gate. Men like Xue Ji and Zhao Xianke, though clever and adaptable, do not transmit the great Way handed down from Xuan, Qi, and Zhongjing.

sentences.zh: 古人云：'不知十二經絡，開口舉手便錯；

translations.literal: The ancients said: 'Not knowing the twelve channels and collaterals, open the mouth and lift the hand and you err;
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: 'Not knowing the twelve channels and collaterals, open the mouth and lift the hand and you err;

sentences.zh: 不明五運六氣，讀盡方書無濟。

translations.literal: not understanding the five movements and six qi, read all formularies to no avail.
translations.idiomatic: not understanding the five movements and six qi, read all formularies to no avail.

sentences.zh: 病有標有本，求其標，只取本，治千人，無一損。

translations.literal: Disease has branch and root; seek the branch but only take the root—treat a thousand people without one harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Disease has branch and root; seek the branch but only take the root—treat a thousand people without one harmed.

sentences.zh: '故示正道，以斥旁門，使學者知所慎。」

translations.literal: Therefore he showed the correct Way to rebuke side gates, so students would know what to heed."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he showed the correct Way to rebuke side gates, so students would know what to heed."

sentences.zh: 後有張錫駒，字令韶，亦錢塘人。

translations.literal: Later came Zhang Xiju, courtesy name Lingshao, also of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Later came Zhang Xiju, courtesy name Lingshao, also of Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 著傷寒論直解、胃氣論，其學本於志聰。

translations.literal: He wrote Straight Commentary on Cold Damage and Treatise on Stomach Qi; his learning derives from Zhicong.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Straight Commentary on Cold Damage and Treatise on Stomach Qi; his learning derives from Zhicong.

sentences.zh: 陳念祖，字修園，福建長樂人​​。

translations.literal: Chen Nianzu, courtesy name Xiuyuan, a native of Changle in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Nianzu, courtesy name Xiuyuan, was a native of Changle in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十七年舉人。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate in the fifty-seventh year of the Qianlong reign.
translations.idiomatic: He was a provincial graduate in the fifty-seventh year of the Qianlong reign.

sentences.zh: 著傷寒金匱淺注，本志聰、錫駒之說，多有發明，世稱善本。

translations.literal: He wrote Brief Commentary on Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer, based on Zhicong and Xiju with many discoveries; the age called it a fine edition.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Brief Commentary on Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer, based on Zhicong and Xiju with many discoveries—the age called it a fine edition.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶中，官直隸威縣知縣，有賢聲。

translations.literal: In the Jiaqing reign he served as magistrate of Wei County in Zhili and had a reputation for worth.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiaqing reign he served as magistrate of Wei County in Zhili and had a reputation for worth.

sentences.zh: 值水災，大疫，親施方藥，活人無算。

translations.literal: When flood and great epidemic struck, he personally dispensed formulas and medicine and saved countless lives.
translations.idiomatic: When flood and great epidemic struck, he personally dispensed formulas and medicine and saved countless lives.

sentences.zh: 晚歸田，以醫學教授，門弟子甚眾，著書凡十餘種，並行世。

translations.literal: In old age he returned to his fields and taught medicine; he had many disciples and more than ten kinds of books, all circulating.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he returned to his fields and taught medicine. He had many disciples and more than ten kinds of books, all circulating.

sentences.zh: 黃元禦，字坤載，山東昌邑人。

translations.literal: Huang Yuanyu, courtesy name Kunzai, a native of Changyi in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Yuanyu, courtesy name Kunzai, was a native of Changyi in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 因庸醫誤藥損目，發憤學醫，於素問、靈樞、難經、傷寒論、金匱玉函經皆有註釋，凡數十萬言。

translations.literal: Because a mediocre physician's mistaken medicine harmed his eyes, he vowed in anger to study medicine and commented on Suwen, Lingshu, the Difficult Classic, Cold Damage, and the Golden Coffer Jade Box Classic, totaling hundreds of thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: Because a mediocre physician's mistaken medicine harmed his eyes, he vowed in anger to study medicine. He commented on Suwen, Lingshu, the Difficult Classic, Cold Damage, and the Golden Coffer Jade Box Classic, totaling hundreds of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 自命甚高，喜更改古書，以伸己說。

translations.literal: He thought very highly of himself and liked to alter ancient books to extend his own sayings.
translations.idiomatic: He thought very highly of himself and liked to alter ancient books to extend his own sayings.

sentences.zh: 其論治病，主於扶陽以抑陰。

translations.literal: In treating disease he chiefly supported yang to restrain yin.
translations.idiomatic: In treating disease he chiefly supported yang to restrain yin.

sentences.zh: 柯琴，字韻伯，浙江慈谿人。

translations.literal: Ke Qin, courtesy name Yunbo, a native of Cixi in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Qin, courtesy name Yunbo, was a native of Cixi in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 博學多聞，能詩、古文辭。

translations.literal: Learned and widely informed, he could write poetry and ancient-style prose.
translations.idiomatic: Learned and widely informed, he could write poetry and ancient-style prose.

sentences.zh: 棄舉子業，矢志醫學。

translations.literal: He abandoned the examination career and devoted himself to medicine.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned the examination career and devoted himself to medicine.

sentences.zh: 家貧，遊吳，棲息於虞山，不以醫自鳴，當世亦鮮知者。

translations.literal: Poor in family, he traveled to Wu and lived on Yushan, not making a name as physician; his age scarcely knew him.
translations.idiomatic: Poor in family, he traveled to Wu and lived on Yushan, not making a name as physician, and his age scarcely knew him.

sentences.zh: 著內經合璧，多所校正，書佚不傳。

translations.literal: He wrote Combined Jade of the Inner Canon, with many corrections; the book is lost and does not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Combined Jade of the Inner Canon, with many corrections; the book is lost and does not circulate.

sentences.zh: 注傷寒論，名曰來蘇集。

translations.literal: He commented on Cold Damage, calling it the Collection for Revival.
translations.idiomatic: He commented on Cold Damage under the title Collection for Revival.

sentences.zh: 以方有執、喻昌等各以己意更定，有背仲景之旨，乃據論中有太陽證、桂枝證、柴胡證諸辭以證名篇，匯集六經諸論，各以類從。

translations.literal: Fang Youzhi, Yu Chang, and others each revised according to their own ideas, departing from Zhongjing's aim; he therefore took the treatise's terms such as taiyang pattern, cinnamon twig pattern, and bupleurum pattern as proof for naming chapters, gathering the six-channel discourses each by kind.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Youzhi, Yu Chang, and others had each revised according to their own ideas, departing from Zhongjing's aim. He therefore took the treatise's terms such as taiyang pattern, cinnamon twig pattern, and bupleurum pattern as proof for naming chapters, gathering the six-channel discourses each by kind.

sentences.zh: 自序略曰：「傷寒論經王叔和編次，已非仲景之舊，讀者必細勘何者為仲景言，何者為叔和筆。

translations.literal: His preface in brief says: "Cold Damage was arranged by Wang Shuhe and is no longer Zhongjing's original; readers must carefully distinguish what is Zhongjing's speech and what is Shuhe's pen.
translations.idiomatic: His preface in brief says: "Cold Damage was arranged by Wang Shuhe and is no longer Zhongjing's original. Readers must carefully distinguish what is Zhongjing's speech and what is Shuhe's pen.

sentences.zh: 其間脫落、倒句、訛字、衍文，一一指破，頓見真面。

translations.literal: Among them omissions, inverted sentences, erroneous characters, and interpolated text are each pointed out, and the true face suddenly appears.
translations.idiomatic: Among them omissions, inverted sentences, erroneous characters, and interpolated text are each pointed out, and the true face suddenly appears.

sentences.zh: 且筆法詳略不同，或互文見意，或比類相形，因此悟彼，見微知著，得於語言文字之外，始可羽翼仲景。

translations.literal: Moreover the brushwork differs in detail and summary, or mutual text shows meaning, or comparison by kind shows form—thus understanding that from this, seeing the subtle and knowing the manifest, obtaining beyond language and writing, only then may one support Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the brushwork differs in detail and summary, or mutual text shows meaning, or comparison by kind shows form—thus understanding that from this, seeing the subtle and knowing the manifest, obtaining beyond language and writing, only then may one support Zhongjing.

sentences.zh: 自來注家，不將全書始終理會，先後合參，隨文敷衍，彼此矛盾，黑白不分。

translations.literal: Former commentators did not reconcile the whole book from beginning to end, early and late together, but glossed as they went, contradicting each other, black and white undivided.
translations.idiomatic: Former commentators did not reconcile the whole book from beginning to end, early and late together, but glossed as they went, contradicting each other, black and white undivided.

sentences.zh: 三百九十七法，不見於仲景序文，又不見於叔和序例，林氏倡於前，成氏和於後，其不足取信，王安道已辨之矣。

translations.literal: The three hundred ninety-seven methods appear neither in Zhongjing's preface nor in Shuhe's preface and arrangement; Lin initiated it before and Cheng followed after—their untrustworthiness Wang Andao already distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: The three hundred ninety-seven methods appear neither in Zhongjing's preface nor in Shuhe's preface and arrangement. Lin initiated it before and Cheng followed after—their untrustworthiness Wang Andao already distinguished.

sentences.zh: 繼起者，猶瑣瑣於數目，亦何補於古人？

translations.literal: Those who came after still fussed over numbers—what help to the ancients?
translations.idiomatic: Those who came after still fussed over numbers—what help to the ancients?

sentences.zh: 何功於後學哉？

translations.literal: What merit for later students?
translations.idiomatic: What merit for later students?

sentences.zh: 大青龍湯，仲景為傷寒中風無汗而兼煩燥者設，即加味麻黃湯耳。

translations.literal: Major Blue Dragon Decoction Zhongjing devised for cold damage and wind stroke without sweat with vexation and dryness—it is merely Ephedra Decoction with additions.
translations.idiomatic: Major Blue Dragon Decoction Zhongjing devised for cold damage and wind stroke without sweat with vexation and dryness—it is merely Ephedra Decoction with additions.

sentences.zh: 而謂其傷寒見風、傷風見寒，因以麻黃湯主寒傷營、桂枝湯主風傷衛、大青龍湯主風寒兩傷營衛，曲成三綱鼎立之說，此鄭聲之亂雅樂也。

translations.literal: Yet they say that in cold damage one sees wind and in wind stroke one sees cold, and thus Ephedra Decoction governs cold injuring constructive, Cinnamon Twig governs wind injuring defensive, Major Blue Dragon governs wind and cold both injuring constructive and defensive—twisting this into the threefold tripod doctrine is Zheng sound disordering elegant music.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they say that in cold damage one sees wind and in wind stroke one sees cold, and thus Ephedra Decoction governs cold injuring constructive, Cinnamon Twig governs wind injuring defensive, Major Blue Dragon governs wind and cold both injuring constructive and defensive—twisting this into the threefold tripod doctrine is vulgar doctrine disordering the classic music.

sentences.zh: 且以十存二三之文，而謂之全篇，手足厥冷之厥，或混於兩陰交盡之厥，其間差謬，何可殫舉？

translations.literal: Moreover with text only one or two tenths remaining they call it the complete scroll; the reversal of cold limbs sometimes confused with reversal at exhaustion of both yin—the errors between cannot be fully listed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover with only one or two tenths of the text remaining they call it the complete scroll. The reversal of cold limbs is sometimes confused with reversal at exhaustion of both yin—the errors cannot be fully listed.

sentences.zh: 此愚所以執卷長吁，不能已也！」

translations.literal: This is why I hold the scroll and sigh long, unable to stop!"
translations.idiomatic: This is why I hold the scroll and sigh long, unable to stop!"

sentences.zh: 又著傷寒論翼，自序略曰：「仲景著傷寒、雜病論，合十六卷，法大備。

translations.literal: He also wrote Wings on Cold Damage; his preface in brief says: "Zhongjing wrote Treatises on Cold Damage and Miscellaneous Disease, sixteen scrolls in all, with methods fully prepared.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Wings on Cold Damage. His preface in brief says: "Zhongjing wrote Treatises on Cold Damage and Miscellaneous Disease, sixteen scrolls in all, with methods fully prepared.

sentences.zh: 其常中之變，變中之常，靡不曲盡。

translations.literal: The constant within change and change within the constant—none is not fully traced.
translations.idiomatic: The constant within change and change within the constant—none is not fully traced.

sentences.zh: 使全書俱在，盡可見論知源。

translations.literal: Had the whole book remained, one could see the treatise and know the source.
translations.idiomatic: Had the whole book remained, one could see the treatise and know the source.

sentences.zh: 自叔和編次傷寒、雜病，分為兩書，然本論中雜病留而未去者尚多，雖有傷寒論之專名，終不失雜病合論之根蒂也。

translations.literal: Since Shuhe arranged cold damage and miscellaneous disease into two books, yet many miscellaneous diseases left undivided remain in the root treatise; though there is the specialized name Cold Damage, it never loses the root of combined discussion of miscellaneous disease.
translations.idiomatic: Since Shuhe arranged cold damage and miscellaneous disease into two books, yet many miscellaneous diseases left undivided remain in the root treatise. Though there is the specialized name Cold Damage, it never loses the root of combined discussion of miscellaneous disease.

sentences.zh: 名不副實，並相淆混，而旁門歧路，莫知所從，豈非叔和之謬以禍之歟？

translations.literal: The name does not match the reality, and they are confused together; side gates and forked paths—none knows which to follow. Is this not Shuhe's error bringing calamity?
translations.idiomatic: The name does not match the reality, and they are confused together. Side gates and forked paths—none knows which to follow. Is this not Shuhe's error bringing calamity?

sentences.zh: 夫仲景之言六經為百病之法，不專為傷寒一科，傷寒、雜病，治無二理，咸歸六經之節制。

translations.literal: Now Zhongjing's saying that the six channels are the method for all diseases is not specialized for cold damage alone; cold damage and miscellaneous disease have no two principles—all obey the six channels' regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongjing said the six channels are the method for all diseases, not specialized for cold damage alone. Cold damage and miscellaneous disease share one principle, all obeying the six channels' regulation.

sentences.zh: 治傷寒者，但拘傷寒，不究其中有雜病之理；

translations.literal: Those who treat cold damage only cling to cold damage and do not investigate the miscellaneous disease principles within;
translations.idiomatic: Those who treat cold damage only cling to cold damage and do not investigate the miscellaneous-disease principles within;

sentences.zh: 治雜病者，復以傷寒論無關於雜病，而置之不問。

translations.literal: those who treat miscellaneous disease again say Cold Damage has nothing to do with miscellaneous disease and set it aside unasked.
translations.idiomatic: those who treat miscellaneous disease again say Cold Damage has nothing to do with miscellaneous disease and set it aside unasked.

sentences.zh: 將參贊化育之書，悉歸狐疑之域，愚甚為斯道憂之。」

translations.literal: They bring books that assist transforming and nourishing entirely into the realm of doubt—I deeply worry for this Way."
translations.idiomatic: They bring books that assist transforming and nourishing entirely into the realm of doubt—I deeply worry for this Way."

sentences.zh: 論者謂琴二書，大有功於仲景。

translations.literal: Critics say Qin's two books greatly served Zhongjing.
translations.idiomatic: Critics say Qin's two books greatly served Zhongjing.

sentences.zh: 尤怡，字在涇，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: You Yi, courtesy name Zaijing, a native of Wu County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: You Yi, courtesy name Zaijing, was a native of Wu County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父有田千畝，至怡中落。

translations.literal: His father had a thousand mu of fields; by Yi's time they had declined.
translations.idiomatic: His father had a thousand mu of fields; by Yi's time they had declined.

sentences.zh: 貧甚，鬻字於佛寺。

translations.literal: Very poor, he sold his writing at Buddhist temples.
translations.idiomatic: Very poor, he sold his writing at Buddhist temples.

sentences.zh: 業醫，人未之異也。

translations.literal: He practiced medicine; people did not think him unusual.
translations.idiomatic: He practiced medicine, but people did not think him unusual.

sentences.zh: 好為詩，與同里顧嗣立、沈德潛游。

translations.literal: Fond of poetry, he associated with Gu Sili and Shen Deqian of the same district.
translations.idiomatic: Fond of poetry, he associated with Gu Sili and Shen Deqian of the same district.

sentences.zh: 晚年，學益深造，治病多奇中，名始著。

translations.literal: In old age his learning went deeper; his cures were often miraculously effective and his name became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: In old age his learning went deeper. His cures were often miraculously effective and his name became renowned.

sentences.zh: 性淡榮利，隱於花溪，自號飼鶴山人，著書自得。

translations.literal: By nature indifferent to glory and profit, he hid on Flower Stream, called himself the Recluse Who Feeds Cranes, and wrote books at his pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: By nature indifferent to glory and profit, he hid on Flower Stream, called himself the Recluse Who Feeds Cranes, and wrote books at his pleasure.

sentences.zh: 其註傷寒論，名曰貫珠集。

translations.literal: His commentary on Cold Damage is called the Stringed Pearl Collection.
translations.idiomatic: His commentary on Cold Damage is called the Stringed Pearl Collection.

sentences.zh: 謂後人因王叔和編次錯亂，辨駁改訂，各成一家言，言愈多而理愈晦。

translations.literal: He said later people, because Wang Shuhe's arrangement was confused, debated and revised, each forming a school—more words made the principle more obscure.
translations.idiomatic: He said later people, because Wang Shuhe's arrangement was confused, debated and revised, each forming a school—more words only made the principle more obscure.

sentences.zh: 乃就六經，各提其綱，於正治法之外，太陽有權變法，斡旋法，救逆法，類病法；

translations.literal: He therefore took the six channels and raised the main thread of each; beyond the regular treatment methods, for taiyang there are expedient, mediating, rescue, and analogous disease methods;
translations.idiomatic: He therefore took the six channels and raised the main thread of each. Beyond the regular treatment methods, for taiyang there are expedient, mediating, rescue, and analogous disease methods;

sentences.zh: 陽明有明辨法，雜治法；

translations.literal: for yangming, discerning and mixed treatment methods;
translations.idiomatic: for yangming, discerning and mixed treatment methods;

sentences.zh: 少陽有權變法；

translations.literal: for shaoyang, expedient methods;
translations.idiomatic: for shaoyang, expedient methods;

sentences.zh: 太陰有藏病、經病法，經、藏俱病法；

translations.literal: for taiyin, visceral disease, channel disease, and both channel and visceral disease methods;
translations.idiomatic: for taiyin, visceral disease, channel disease, and both channel and visceral disease methods;

sentences.zh: 少陰、厥陰有溫法、凊法。

translations.literal: for shaoyin and jueyin, warming and cooling methods.
translations.idiomatic: for shaoyin and jueyin, warming and cooling methods.

sentences.zh: 凡病機進退微權，各有法以為辨，使讀者先得其法，乃能用其方。

translations.literal: Every subtle turn of disease mechanism advance and retreat has a method for discrimination, so readers first obtain the method and then can use the formulas.
translations.idiomatic: Every subtle turn of disease mechanism advance and retreat has a method for discrimination, so readers first obtain the method and then can use the formulas.

sentences.zh: 分證甚晰，於少陰、厥陰、溫凊兩法，尤足破世人之惑。

translations.literal: Pattern division is very clear; on shaoyin, jueyin, and the two methods of warming and cooling, it especially breaks worldly confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Pattern division is very clear. On shaoyin, jueyin, and the two methods of warming and cooling, it especially breaks worldly confusion.

sentences.zh: 注金匱要略，名曰心典。

translations.literal: He commented on the Essentials of the Golden Coffer, calling it the Heart Canon.
translations.idiomatic: He commented on the Essentials of the Golden Coffer under the title Heart Canon.

sentences.zh: 別撰集諸家方書、雜病治要，足以羽翼仲景者，論其精蘊，曰金匱翼。

translations.literal: Separately he compiled various schools' formularies and Essentials for Treating Miscellaneous Disease, enough to support Zhongjing, discussing their essence in Golden Coffer Wings.
translations.idiomatic: Separately he compiled various schools' formularies and Essentials for Treating Miscellaneous Disease, enough to support Zhongjing, discussing their essence in Golden Coffer Wings.

sentences.zh: 又著醫學讀書記，於軒、岐以下諸家，多有折衷，徐大椿稱為得古人意。

translations.literal: He also wrote Notes on Reading Medicine, with much reconciliation among schools from Xuan and Qi down; Xu Dachun said it obtained the ancients' meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Notes on Reading Medicine, with much reconciliation among schools from Xuan and Qi down. Xu Dachun said it obtained the ancients' meaning.

sentences.zh: 怡著述並篤雅，世以貫珠集與柯琴來蘇集並重焉。

translations.literal: Yi's writings are all refined; the age ranks the Stringed Pearl Collection with Qin's Collection for Revival.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's writings are all refined; the age ranks the Stringed Pearl Collection with Qin's Collection for Revival.

sentences.zh: 葉桂，字天士，江蘇吳縣人。

translations.literal: Ye Gui, courtesy name Tianshi, a native of Wu County in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Gui, courtesy name Tianshi, was a native of Wu County in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 先世自歙遷吳，祖時、父朝採，皆精醫。

translations.literal: His forebears moved from She to Wu; his grandfather Shi and father Chaocai were both skilled in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears moved from She to Wu. His grandfather Shi and father Chaocai were both skilled in medicine.

sentences.zh: 桂年十四喪父，從學於父之門人，聞言即解，見出師上，遂有聞於時。

translations.literal: Gui at fourteen lost his father and studied with his father's disciples; hearing a word he understood, and when he surpassed his teacher he was heard of in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Gui at fourteen lost his father and studied with his father's disciples. Hearing a word he understood, and when he surpassed his teacher he was heard of in the age.

sentences.zh: 切脈望色，如見五藏。

translations.literal: Taking the pulse and observing color, it was as if he saw the five viscera.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the pulse and observing color, it was as if he saw the five viscera.

sentences.zh: 治方不出成見，嘗曰：「劑之寒溫視乎病，前人或偏寒涼，或偏溫養，習者茫無定識。

translations.literal: His treatment formulas did not go beyond established views; he once said: "Whether a formula is cold or warm depends on the disease; former men were sometimes partial to cold and cool, sometimes partial to warm nourishment, and learners had no fixed knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: His treatment formulas did not go beyond established views. He once said: "Whether a formula is cold or warm depends on the disease. Former men were sometimes partial to cold and cool, sometimes partial to warm nourishment, and learners had no fixed knowledge.

sentences.zh: 假兼備以幸中，借和平以藏拙。

translations.literal: Some feign comprehensiveness to hope to hit, some borrow harmony to hide incompetence.
translations.idiomatic: Some feign comprehensiveness to hope to hit; some borrow harmony to hide incompetence.

sentences.zh: 朝用一方。

translations.literal: Using one formula in the morning.
translations.idiomatic: Using one formula in the morning.

sentences.zh: 晚易一劑，詎有當哉？

translations.literal: Changing to another dose in the evening—how can that be right?
translations.idiomatic: Changing to another dose in the evening—how can that be right?

sentences.zh: 病有見證，有變證，必胸有成竹，乃可施之以方。」

translations.literal: Disease has manifest pattern and changing pattern; one must have a complete plan in the breast before applying a formula."
translations.idiomatic: Disease has manifest pattern and changing pattern; one must have a complete plan in the breast before applying a formula."

sentences.zh: 其治病多奇中，於疑難證，或就其平日嗜好而得救法；

translations.literal: His cures were often miraculously effective; for doubtful difficult patterns he sometimes obtained the method of cure from the patient's daily habits;
translations.idiomatic: His cures were often miraculously effective. For doubtful difficult patterns he sometimes obtained the method of cure from the patient's daily habits;

sentences.zh: 或他醫之方，略與變通服法；

translations.literal: or another physician's formula, slightly altered in method of taking;
translations.idiomatic: or another physician's formula, slightly altered in method of taking;

sentences.zh: 或竟不與藥，而使居處飲食消息之；

translations.literal: or he gave no medicine at all but had them regulate dwelling, food, and drink;
translations.idiomatic: or he gave no medicine at all but had them regulate dwelling, food, and drink;

sentences.zh: 或於無病時預知其病；

translations.literal: or when without disease he foreknew the disease;
translations.idiomatic: or when without disease he foreknew the disease;

sentences.zh: 或預斷數十年後：皆驗。

translations.literal: or foretold decades later—all verified.
translations.idiomatic: or foretold decades later—all verified.

sentences.zh: 當時名滿天下，傳聞附會，往往涉於荒誕，不具錄。

translations.literal: His name filled the world; attached rumors often touched the absurd and are not fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: His name filled the world; attached rumors often touched the absurd and are not fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 卒，年八十。

translations.literal: He died at eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 臨歿，戒其子曰：「醫可為而不可為。

translations.literal: On the verge of death he admonished his son: "Medicine may be practiced but may not be practiced.
translations.idiomatic: On the verge of death he admonished his son: "Medicine may be practiced but may not be practiced.

sentences.zh: 必天資敏悟，讀萬卷書，而後可以濟世。

translations.literal: One must be gifted with keen intelligence and read ten thousand scrolls before one can benefit the world.
translations.idiomatic: One must be gifted with keen intelligence and read ten thousand scrolls before one can benefit the world.

sentences.zh: 不然，鮮有不殺人者，是以藥餌為刀刃也。

translations.literal: Otherwise few do not kill; thus drugs and formulas are blades.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise few do not kill; thus drugs and formulas are blades.

sentences.zh: 吾死，子孫慎勿輕言醫！」

translations.literal: When I die, descendants must not lightly speak of medicine!"
translations.idiomatic: When I die, descendants must not lightly speak of medicine!"

sentences.zh: 桂神悟絕人，貫徹古今醫術，而鮮著述。

translations.literal: Gui's divine insight surpassed others; he penetrated medical arts ancient and modern, yet wrote little.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's divine insight surpassed others. He penetrated medical arts ancient and modern, yet wrote little.

sentences.zh: 世傳所注本草，多心得。

translations.literal: The materia medica commentary attributed to him has many insights.
translations.idiomatic: The materia medica commentary attributed to him has many insights.

sentences.zh: 又許叔微本事方釋義、景岳發揮。

translations.literal: Also Xu Shuxi's Commentary on Effective Formulas and Elaboration on Jingyue.
translations.idiomatic: Also Xu Shuxi's Commentary on Effective Formulas and Elaboration on Jingyue.

sentences.zh: 歿後，門人集醫案為臨證指南，非其自著。

translations.literal: After death his disciples collected medical cases as Guide to Clinical Pattern— not his own composition.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his disciples collected medical cases as Guide to Clinical Pattern—not his own composition.

sentences.zh: 附幼科心法一卷，傳為桂手定，徐大椿謂獨精卓，後章楠改題曰三時伏氣外感篇；

translations.literal: Appended is one scroll of Pediatric Heart Method, transmitted as fixed by Gui's hand; Xu Dachun said it alone is exquisite, and later Zhang Nan retitled it Treatise on External Heat in the Three Seasons;
translations.idiomatic: Appended is one scroll of Pediatric Heart Method, transmitted as fixed by Gui's hand. Xu Dachun said it alone is exquisite, and later Zhang Nan retitled it Treatise on External Heat in the Three Seasons;

sentences.zh: 又附溫證證治一卷，傳為口授門人顧景文者，楠改題曰外感溫證篇。

translations.literal: also appended is one scroll on warm pattern treatment, transmitted as orally taught to disciple Gu Jingwen; Nan retitled it Treatise on External Warm Patterns.
translations.idiomatic: also appended is one scroll on warm pattern treatment, transmitted as orally taught to disciple Gu Jingwen; Nan retitled it Treatise on External Warm Patterns.

sentences.zh: 二書最為學者所奉習。

translations.literal: These two books students most revere and practice.
