translations.idiomatic: These two books students most revere and practice.

sentences.zh: 同里薛雪，名亞於桂，而大江南、北，言醫輒以桂為宗，百餘年來，私淑者眾。

translations.literal: Xue Xue of the same district, his name below Gui's, yet south and north of the great rivers, speaking of medicine always took Gui as patriarch; for more than a hundred years private followers were many.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Xue of the same district ranked below Gui in name, yet south and north of the great rivers, speaking of medicine always took Gui as patriarch. For more than a hundred years private followers were many.

sentences.zh: 最著者，吳瑭、章楠、王士雄。

translations.literal: The most renowned: Wu Tang, Zhang Nan, and Wang Shixiong.
translations.idiomatic: The most renowned were Wu Tang, Zhang Nan, and Wang Shixiong.

sentences.zh: 雪，字生白，自號一瓢。

translations.literal: Xue, courtesy name Shengbai, sobriquet One Gourd.
translations.idiomatic: Xue, courtesy name Shengbai, sobriquet One Gourd.

sentences.zh: 少學詩於同郡葉燮。

translations.literal: In youth he studied poetry under Ye Xie of the same commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied poetry under Ye Xie of the same commandery.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，舉鴻博，未遇。

translations.literal: In early Qianlong he was nominated for the Boxue examination but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In early Qianlong he was nominated for the Boxue examination but did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 工畫蘭，善拳勇，博學多通，於醫時有獨見。

translations.literal: Skilled at painting orchids and martial arts, broadly learned and versatile, in medicine he often had unique views.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at painting orchids and martial arts, broadly learned and versatile, and in medicine he often had unique views.

sentences.zh: 斷人生死不爽，療治多異跡。

translations.literal: Judging life and death without error, his cures had many marvels.
translations.idiomatic: He judged life and death without error, and his cures had many marvels.

sentences.zh: 生平與桂不相能，自名所居曰掃葉莊，然每見桂處方而善，未嘗不擊節也。

translations.literal: All his life he did not get along with Gui; he named his dwelling Sweeping Leaves Villa, yet whenever he saw Gui's prescriptions he admired them and never failed to applaud.
translations.idiomatic: All his life he did not get along with Gui. He named his dwelling Sweeping Leaves Villa, yet whenever he saw Gui's prescriptions he admired them and never failed to applaud.

sentences.zh: 著醫經原旨，於靈、素奧旨，具有發揮。

translations.literal: He wrote Origins of the Medical Canon, with real development of the subtle aims of Lingshu and Suwen.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Origins of the Medical Canon, with real development of the subtle aims of Lingshu and Suwen.

sentences.zh: 世傳濕溫篇，為學者所宗，或曰非雪作。

translations.literal: The Warm-Damp Treatise transmitted in the world is revered by students; some say it is not Xue's work.
translations.idiomatic: The Warm-Damp Treatise transmitted in the world is revered by students; some say it is not Xue's work.

sentences.zh: 其醫案與桂及繆遵義合刻。

translations.literal: His medical cases were printed together with Gui's and Miao Zunyi's.
translations.idiomatic: His medical cases were printed together with Gui's and Miao Zunyi's.

sentences.zh: 遵義，亦吳人。

translations.literal: Zunyi was also a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Zunyi was also a man of Wu.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二年進士，官知縣。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Qianlong, served as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He became jinshi in the second year of Qianlong and served as magistrate.

sentences.zh: 因母病，通方書，棄官為醫，用藥每出創意，吳中稱三家焉。

translations.literal: Because his mother fell ill he mastered formularies, abandoned office for medicine, and his use of drugs often showed original ideas; Wu called them the three masters.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mother fell ill he mastered formularies, abandoned office for medicine, and his use of drugs often showed original ideas. Wu called them the three masters.

sentences.zh: 瑭，字鞠通，江蘇淮陰人。

translations.literal: Tang, courtesy name Jutong, a native of Huaiyin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, courtesy name Jutong, was a native of Huaiyin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 乾、嘉之間遊京師，有名。

translations.literal: Between Qianlong and Jiaqing he traveled the capital and was renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Between Qianlong and Jiaqing he traveled the capital and was renowned.

sentences.zh: 學本於桂，以桂立論甚簡，但有醫案散見於雜證之中，人多忽之。

translations.literal: His learning derived from Gui; Gui's doctrine was very brief, but medical cases scattered among miscellaneous patterns were often overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: His learning derived from Gui. Gui's doctrine was very brief, but medical cases scattered among miscellaneous patterns were often overlooked.

sentences.zh: 著溫病條辨，以暢其義，其書盛行。

translations.literal: He wrote Detailed Differentiation of Warm Disease to expound the meaning; the book flourished.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Detailed Differentiation of Warm Disease to expound the meaning, and the book flourished.

sentences.zh: 同時歸安吳貞，著傷寒指掌，亦發明桂醫案之旨，與瑭相同。

translations.literal: At the same time Wu Zhen of Gui'an wrote Finger Guide to Cold Damage, also developing Gui's medical cases, the same as Tang.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Wu Zhen of Gui'an wrote Finger Guide to Cold Damage, also developing Gui's medical cases, the same as Tang.

sentences.zh: 楠，字虛谷，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Nan, courtesy name Xugu, a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Nan, courtesy name Xugu, was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 著醫門棒喝。

translations.literal: He wrote Awakening Cry in the Medical Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Awakening Cry in the Medical Gate.

sentences.zh: 謂桂、雪最得仲景遺意，而他家不與。

translations.literal: He said Gui and Xue most obtained Zhongjing's legacy, and other schools did not.
translations.idiomatic: He said Gui and Xue most obtained Zhongjing's legacy, and other schools did not.

sentences.zh: 士雄，字孟英，浙江海寧人。

translations.literal: Shixiong, courtesy name Mengying, a native of Haining in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong, courtesy name Mengying, was a native of Haining in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 居於杭，世為醫。

translations.literal: He lived in Hangzhou; the family practiced medicine for generations.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Hangzhou; the family practiced medicine for generations.

sentences.zh: 士雄讀書礪行，家貧，仍以醫自給。

translations.literal: Shixiong read books and cultivated conduct; though poor he still supported himself by medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong read books and cultivated conduct. Though poor he still supported himself by medicine.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，杭州陷，轉徙上海。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng reign Hangzhou fell; he moved to Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng reign Hangzhou fell, and he moved to Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 時吳、越避寇者麕集，疫癘大作，士雄療治，多全活。

translations.literal: Then refugees from Wu and Yue gathered; pestilence broke out greatly; Shixiong treated and mostly saved lives.
translations.idiomatic: Then refugees from Wu and Yue gathered and pestilence broke out greatly. Shixiong treated them and mostly saved lives.

sentences.zh: 舊著霍亂論，致慎於溫補，至是重訂刊行，醫者奉為圭臬。

translations.literal: He had formerly written Treatise on Cholera, warning against warm supplementation; now he revised and published it, and physicians took it as standard.
translations.idiomatic: He had formerly written Treatise on Cholera, warning against warm supplementation. Now he revised and published it, and physicians took it as standard.

sentences.zh: 又著溫熱經緯，以軒、岐、仲景之文為經，葉、薛諸家之辨為緯，大意同章楠註釋。

translations.literal: He also wrote Warp and Woof of Warm Heat, taking Xuan, Qi, and Zhongjing as warp and Ye and Xue's differentiations as woof, the main idea like Nan's commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote Warp and Woof of Warm Heat, taking Xuan, Qi, and Zhongjing as warp and Ye and Xue's differentiations as woof—the main idea like Nan's commentary.

sentences.zh: 兼採昔賢諸說，擇善而從，勝楠書。

translations.literal: Also gathering former worthies' sayings, choosing the good and following, it surpasses Nan's book.
translations.idiomatic: Also gathering former worthies' sayings and choosing the good, it surpasses Nan's book.

sentences.zh: 所著凡數種，以二者為精詳。

translations.literal: His writings number several kinds; these two are most detailed.
translations.idiomatic: His writings number several kinds; these two are most detailed.

sentences.zh: 同時浙西論醫者，平湖陸以湉、嘉善汪震、烏程汪曰楨，宗旨略同。

translations.literal: At the same time in western Zhejiang discussing medicine were Lu Yitian of Pinghu, Wang Zhen of Jiashan, and Wang Rizhen of Wucheng, their aims roughly the same.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time in western Zhejiang discussing medicine were Lu Yitian of Pinghu, Wang Zhen of Jiashan, and Wang Rizhen of Wucheng, their aims roughly the same.

sentences.zh: 陽湖張琦、曜孫，父子皆通儒，以醫鳴，取黃元禦扶陽之說，偏於溫。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi and his son Yaosun of Yanghu were both Confucian scholars famed in medicine, taking Huang Yuanyu's yang-supporting doctrine, partial to warmth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi and his son Yaosun of Yanghu were both Confucian scholars famed in medicine, taking Huang Yuanyu's yang-supporting doctrine and partial to warmth.

sentences.zh: 曜孫至上海，或勸士雄往就正，士雄謝之。

translations.literal: Yaosun came to Shanghai; some urged Shixiong to go seek correction; Shixiong declined.
translations.idiomatic: Yaosun came to Shanghai; some urged Shixiong to go seek correction, but Shixiong declined.

sentences.zh: 號葉氏學者，要以士雄為巨擘，惟喜用辛涼，論者謂亦稍偏雲。

translations.literal: Those who called themselves the Ye school chiefly took Shixiong as chief, yet he liked pungent cool; critics said he was also somewhat partial.
translations.idiomatic: Those who called themselves the Ye school chiefly took Shixiong as chief, yet he liked pungent cool drugs; critics said he was also somewhat partial.

sentences.zh: 徐大椿，原名大業，字靈胎，晚號洄溪，江蘇吳江人，翰林檢討釚孫。

translations.literal: Xu Dachun, original name Daye, courtesy name Lingtai, late sobriquet Huixi, a native of Wujiang in Jiangsu, grandson of Hanlin examiner Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Dachun, original name Daye, courtesy name Lingtai, late sobriquet Huixi, was a native of Wujiang in Jiangsu and grandson of Hanlin examiner Xu.

sentences.zh: 生有異禀，長身廣顙，聰強過人。

translations.literal: Born with unusual endowment, tall with broad forehead, clever and strong beyond others.
translations.idiomatic: Born with unusual endowment, he was tall with a broad forehead, clever and strong beyond others.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，勿屑，去而窮經，探研易理，好讀黃老與陰符家言。

translations.literal: A licentiate, he disdained it and left to exhaust the classics, probing the Changes, fond of reading Huang-Lao and yinfu masters.
translations.idiomatic: A licentiate, he disdained it and left to exhaust the classics, probing the Changes and fond of reading Huang-Lao and yinfu masters.

sentences.zh: 凡星經、地志、九宮、音律、技擊、句卒、嬴越之法，靡不通究，尤邃於醫，世多傳其異跡。

translations.literal: Astronomy, geography, nine palaces, pitch and rhythm, martial arts, military science, and methods of Yue—all he thoroughly investigated, especially penetrating in medicine; the world transmitted many marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomy, geography, nine palaces, pitch and rhythm, martial arts, military science, and methods of Yue—all he thoroughly investigated, especially penetrating in medicine, and the world transmitted many marvels.

sentences.zh: 然大椿自編醫案，惟剖析虛實寒溫，發明治療之法，歸於平實，於神異者僅載一二。

translations.literal: Yet Dachun in his own compiled medical cases only analyzed vacuity-repletion and cold-heat, expounding treatment methods, returning to level truth; of marvels he recorded only one or two.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in his own compiled medical cases Dachun only analyzed vacuity-repletion and cold-heat, expounding treatment methods and returning to level truth; of marvels he recorded only one or two.

sentences.zh: 其書世多有，不具錄。

translations.literal: His books are many in the world and are not fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: His books are many in the world and are not fully recorded here.

sentences.zh: 乾隆二十四年，大學士蔣溥病，高宗命徵海內名醫，以薦召入都。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Qianlong Grand Secretary Jiang Pu fell ill; the Gaozong Emperor ordered famous physicians summoned from within the seas; on recommendation Dachun was called to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year of Qianlong Grand Secretary Jiang Pu fell ill. The Gaozong Emperor ordered famous physicians summoned from within the seas, and on recommendation Dachun was called to the capital.

sentences.zh: 大椿奏溥病不可治，上嘉其樸誠，命入太醫院供奉，尋乞歸。

translations.literal: Dachun memorialized that Pu's disease could not be cured; the emperor praised his honesty and ordered him to serve in the Imperial Medical Academy, but he soon begged to return.
translations.idiomatic: Dachun memorialized that Pu's disease could not be cured. The emperor praised his honesty and ordered him to serve in the Imperial Medical Academy, but he soon begged to return.

sentences.zh: 後二十年復詔徵，年已七十九，遂卒於京師，賜金治喪。

translations.literal: Twenty years later he was again summoned by edict; he was already seventy-nine and died in the capital; gold was bestowed for the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty years later he was again summoned by edict. He was already seventy-nine and died in the capital; gold was bestowed for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 大椿學博而通，注神農本草經百種，以舊注但言其當然，不言其所以然，採掇常用之品，備列經文，推闡主治之義，於諸家中最有啟發之功。

translations.literal: Dachun's learning was broad and penetrating; he commented on a hundred kinds in the Divine Farmer's Root Materia Medica—old commentaries only said what was so, not why; he selected commonly used items, fully listed the classic text, and developed the meaning of governing treatment, among all schools most enlightening.
translations.idiomatic: Dachun's learning was broad and penetrating. He commented on a hundred kinds in the Divine Farmer's Root Materia Medica—old commentaries only said what was so, not why. He selected commonly used items, fully listed the classic text, and developed the meaning of governing treatment, among all schools most enlightening.

sentences.zh: 注難經曰經釋，辨其與靈樞、素問說有異同。

translations.literal: He commented on the Difficult Classic, called Canon Explanation, distinguishing where it differs from Lingshu and Suwen.
translations.idiomatic: He commented on the Difficult Classic under the title Canon Explanation, distinguishing where it differs from Lingshu and Suwen.

sentences.zh: 注傷寒曰類方，謂：「醫家刊定傷寒論，如治尚書者之爭洪範、武成，注大學者之爭古本、今本，終無定論。

translations.literal: He commented on Cold Damage, called Classified Formulas, saying: "Medical editors fixing Cold Damage are like those debating Hongfan and Wucheng in the Documents, or ancient versus modern editions of the Great Learning—ultimately no fixed conclusion.
translations.idiomatic: He commented on Cold Damage under the title Classified Formulas, saying: "Medical editors fixing Cold Damage are like those debating Hongfan and Wucheng in the Documents, or ancient versus modern editions of the Great Learning—ultimately no fixed conclusion.

sentences.zh: 不知仲景本論，乃救誤之書，當時隨證立方，本無定序。」

translations.literal: They do not know Zhongjing's root treatise is a book for correcting errors; formulas were made for patterns as they arose, originally without fixed order."
translations.idiomatic: They do not know Zhongjing's root treatise is a book for correcting errors. Formulas were made for patterns as they arose, originally without fixed order."

sentences.zh: 於是削除陰陽六經門目，但使方以類從，證隨方定，使人可案證以求方，而不必循經以求證。

translations.literal: He therefore deleted the yin-yang six-channel categories but grouped formulas by kind and fixed patterns with formulas, so people may seek formulas by pattern without following channels to seek patterns.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore deleted the yin-yang six-channel categories but grouped formulas by kind and fixed patterns with formulas, so people may seek formulas by pattern without following channels to seek patterns.

sentences.zh: 一切葛藤，盡芟去之。

translations.literal: All entanglements were entirely cut away.
translations.idiomatic: All entanglements were entirely cut away.

sentences.zh: 所著蘭台軌範，凡錄病論，惟取靈樞、素問、難經、金匱要略、傷寒論、隋巢元方病源、唐孫思邈千金方、王燾外台秘要而止。

translations.literal: His Orchid Terrace Standards records disease treatises only from Lingshu, Suwen, Difficult Classic, Essentials of the Golden Coffer, Cold Damage, Sui Chao Yuanfang's Origins of Disease, Tang Sun Simiao's Thousand Gold Formulas, and Wang Tao's Secret Essentials of the Outer Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: His Orchid Terrace Standards records disease treatises only from Lingshu, Suwen, Difficult Classic, Essentials of the Golden Coffer, Cold Damage, Sui Chao Yuanfang's Origins of Disease, Tang Sun Simiao's Thousand Gold Formulas, and Wang Tao's Secret Essentials of the Outer Terrace.

sentences.zh: 錄方亦多取諸書，宋以後方，則採其義可推尋、試多獲效者，去取最為謹嚴。

translations.literal: Formulas too are mostly taken from these books; post-Song formulas he took only when the meaning can be traced and trials often succeeded—selection most strict.
translations.idiomatic: Formulas too are mostly taken from these books. Post-Song formulas he took only when the meaning can be traced and trials often succeeded—selection was most strict.

sentences.zh: 於疑似出入之間，辨別尤悉。

translations.literal: On seeming agreement and divergence he discriminated especially fully.
translations.idiomatic: On seeming agreement and divergence he discriminated especially fully.

sentences.zh: 其論醫之書曰醫學源流論，分目九十有三。

translations.literal: His book on medicine is called Treatise on the Sources of Medicine, in ninety-three sections.
translations.idiomatic: His book on medicine is called Treatise on the Sources of Medicine, in ninety-three sections.

sentences.zh: 謂：「病之名有萬，而脈之像不過數十，是必以望、聞、問三者參之。

translations.literal: He said: "Disease names are ten thousand but pulse images are only several tens—one must consult the three of looking, listening, and asking.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Disease names are ten thousand but pulse images are only several tens—one must consult the three of looking, listening, and asking.

sentences.zh: 如病同人異之辨，兼證兼病之別，亡陰亡陽之分。

translations.literal: Such as distinguishing same disease different persons, combined patterns and combined diseases, loss of yin and loss of yang.
translations.idiomatic: Such as distinguishing same disease in different persons, combined patterns and combined diseases, loss of yin and loss of yang.

sentences.zh: 病有不愈不死，有雖愈必死，又有藥誤不即死。

translations.literal: Some diseases do not heal yet do not die; some though healed must die; some from mistaken medicine do not die at once.
translations.idiomatic: Some diseases do not heal yet do not die; some though healed must die; some from mistaken medicine do not die at once.

sentences.zh: 藥性有古今變遷，內經司天運氣之說不可泥。

translations.literal: Drug nature has ancient and modern change; one must not cling to the Inner Canon's doctrine of celestial motion and qi.
translations.idiomatic: Drug nature has ancient and modern change; one must not cling to the Inner Canon's doctrine of celestial motion and qi.

sentences.zh: 針灸之法失傳。」

translations.literal: Acupuncture and moxibustion methods are lost."
translations.idiomatic: Acupuncture and moxibustion methods are lost."

sentences.zh: 諸說並可取。

translations.literal: These sayings are all acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: These sayings are all acceptable.

sentences.zh: 又慎疾芻言，為溺於邪說俗見者痛下針砭，多驚心動魄之語。

translations.literal: Also Cautionary Words on Disease, sharply needling those drowned in heterodox sayings and vulgar views, with many startling words.
translations.idiomatic: Also Cautionary Words on Disease, sharply needling those drowned in heterodox sayings and vulgar views, with many startling words.

sentences.zh: 醫貫砭，專斥趙獻可溫補之弊。

translations.literal: Medical Girdle Needle especially rebukes Zhao Xianke's warm supplementation.
translations.idiomatic: Medical Girdle Needle especially rebukes Zhao Xianke's warm supplementation.

sentences.zh: 諸書並行世。

translations.literal: All books circulate in the world.
translations.idiomatic: All books circulate in the world.

sentences.zh: 大椿與葉桂同以醫名吳中，而宗旨異。

translations.literal: Dachun and Ye Gui were both famed in medicine in Wu, but their aims differed.
translations.idiomatic: Dachun and Ye Gui were both famed in medicine in Wu, but their aims differed.

sentences.zh: 評桂醫案，多所糾正。

translations.literal: In reviewing Gui's medical cases he corrected many points.
translations.idiomatic: In reviewing Gui's medical cases he corrected many points.

sentences.zh: 兼精瘍科，而未著專書，謂世傳外科正宗一書，輕用刀針及毒藥，往往害人，詳為批評，世並奉為善本。

translations.literal: Also skilled in ulcer medicine but without a specialized book; he said the transmitted Orthodox Surgery lightly uses knife, needle, and poisonous drugs and often harms people, and criticized it in detail; the age also took it as a fine edition.
translations.idiomatic: Also skilled in ulcer medicine but without a specialized book. He said the transmitted Orthodox Surgery lightly uses knife, needle, and poisonous drugs and often harms people, and criticized it in detail; the age also took it as a fine edition.

sentences.zh: 同郡吳縣王維德，字洪緒，自號林屋山人。

translations.literal: Wang Weide of the same commandery Wu County, courtesy name Hongxu, sobriquet Recluse of Forest Dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Weide of Wu County in the same commandery, courtesy name Hongxu, sobriquet Recluse of Forest Dwelling.

sentences.zh: 曾祖字若谷，精瘍醫，維德傳其學，著外科全生集。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Ziruogu was skilled in ulcer medicine; Weide inherited the learning and wrote Complete Collection for Saving Life in Surgery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Ziruogu was skilled in ulcer medicine. Weide inherited the learning and wrote Complete Collection for Saving Life in Surgery.

sentences.zh: 謂：「癰疽無死證，癰乃陽實，氣血熱而毒滯；

translations.literal: He said: "Abscess and gangrene have no fatal pattern; abscess is yang repletion, qi and blood hot with stagnant toxin;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Abscess and gangrene have no fatal pattern. Abscess is yang repletion, with qi and blood hot and toxin stagnant;

sentences.zh: 疽乃陰虛，氣血寒而毒凝。

translations.literal: gangrene is yin vacuity, qi and blood cold with congealed toxin.
translations.idiomatic: gangrene is yin vacuity, with qi and blood cold and toxin congealed.

sentences.zh: 皆以開腠理為要，治者但當論陰陽虛實。

translations.literal: Both take opening the interstices as essential; the physician should only discuss yin-yang vacuity and repletion.
translations.idiomatic: Both take opening the interstices as essential; the physician should only discuss yin-yang vacuity and repletion.

sentences.zh: 初起色紅為癰，色白為疽，截然兩途。

translations.literal: At first rise, red color is abscess, white is gangrene—utterly two paths.
translations.idiomatic: At first rise, red color is abscess, white is gangrene—utterly two paths.

sentences.zh: 世人以癰疽連呼並治，誤矣。」

translations.literal: The world calls abscess and gangrene together and treats together—wrong."
translations.idiomatic: The world calls abscess and gangrene together and treats them together—wrong."

sentences.zh: 其論為前人所未發。

translations.literal: His doctrine was what former men had not expounded.
translations.idiomatic: His doctrine was what former men had not expounded.

sentences.zh: 凡治初起以消為貴，以託為畏，尤戒刀針毒藥，與大椿說略同，醫者宗之。

translations.literal: In treating initial rise, dissolving is valued and suppuration feared; knife, needle, and poisonous drugs are especially forbidden—much like Dachun's doctrine; physicians took him as patriarch.
translations.idiomatic: In treating initial rise, dissolving is valued and suppuration feared. Knife, needle, and poisonous drugs are especially forbidden—much like Dachun's doctrine, and physicians took him as patriarch.

sentences.zh: 維德兼通陰陽家言，著永寧通書、卜筮正宗。

translations.literal: Weide also penetrated yin-yang masters' sayings, writing Everlasting Peace Almanac and Orthodox Divination.
translations.idiomatic: Weide also penetrated yin-yang masters' sayings, writing Everlasting Peace Almanac and Orthodox Divination.

sentences.zh: 吳謙，字六吉，安徽歙縣人。

translations.literal: Wu Qian, courtesy name Liuji, a native of She County in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qian, courtesy name Liuji, was a native of She County in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 官太醫院判，供奉內廷，屢被恩賚。

translations.literal: He served as vice-director of the Imperial Medical Academy, attending the inner court, repeatedly favored with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-director of the Imperial Medical Academy, attending the inner court, and was repeatedly favored with gifts.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，敕編醫書，太醫院使錢鬥保請發內府藏書，並徵集天下家藏秘籍，及世傳經驗良方，分門聚類，刪其駁雜，採其精粹，發其餘蘊，補其未備，為書二部。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign an edict ordered medical books compiled; Director Qian Doubao requested inner palace books be issued and secret editions and experiential formulas from families under heaven be gathered, classified by category, rejecting what was confused, taking the essence, developing what remained, supplementing what was lacking—two works.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong reign an edict ordered medical books compiled. Director Qian Doubao requested inner palace books be issued and secret editions and experiential formulas from families under heaven be gathered, classified by category, rejecting what was confused, taking the essence, developing what remained, supplementing what was lacking—two works.

sentences.zh: 小而約者，以為初學誦讀；

translations.literal: The smaller and concise for beginners to recite;
translations.idiomatic: The smaller and concise for beginners to recite;

sentences.zh: 大而博者，以為學成參考。

translations.literal: the larger and broad for accomplished study as reference.
translations.idiomatic: the larger and broad for accomplished study as reference.

sentences.zh: 既而徵書之令中止，議專編一書，期速成，命謙及同官劉裕鐸為總修官。

translations.literal: Later the order to gather books ceased; it was decided to compile one book for quick completion, appointing Qian and colleague Liu Yude as chief editors.
translations.idiomatic: Later the order to gather books ceased. It was decided to compile one book for quick completion, appointing Qian and colleague Liu Yude as chief editors.

sentences.zh: 謙以古醫書有法無方，惟傷寒論、金匱要略、雜病論始有法有方。

translations.literal: Qian said ancient medical books have methods without formulas; only Cold Damage, Essentials of the Golden Coffer, and Treatise on Miscellaneous Disease have both methods and formulas.
translations.idiomatic: Qian said ancient medical books have methods without formulas; only Cold Damage, Essentials of the Golden Coffer, and Treatise on Miscellaneous Disease have both methods and formulas.

sentences.zh: 靈、素而後，二書實一脈相承。

translations.literal: After Lingshu and Suwen, the two books truly inherit one thread.
translations.idiomatic: After Lingshu and Suwen, the two books truly inherit one thread.

sentences.zh: 義理淵深，方法微奧，領會不易，遂多譌錯。

translations.literal: Principle is deep and methods subtle; comprehension is not easy, so there are many errors.
translations.idiomatic: Principle is deep and methods subtle; comprehension is not easy, so there are many errors.

sentences.zh: 舊注隨文附會，難以傳信。

translations.literal: Old commentaries gloss as the text goes and are hard to trust.
translations.idiomatic: Old commentaries gloss as the text goes and are hard to trust.

sentences.zh: 謙自為刪定，書成八九，及是，請就謙未成之書，更加增減。

translations.literal: Qian himself made a revised edition, eight or nine tenths complete; then he was asked to take Qian's unfinished book and further add and subtract.
translations.idiomatic: Qian himself made a revised edition, eight or nine tenths complete; then he was asked to take Qian's unfinished book and further add and subtract.

sentences.zh: 於二書譌錯者，悉為訂正，逐條註釋，复集諸家舊注實足闡發微義者，以資參考，為全書之首，標示正軌。

translations.literal: Errors in the two books were all corrected, line by line commented, and former schools' old notes that truly developed subtle meaning were gathered for reference, as the head of the whole work marking the correct track.
translations.idiomatic: Errors in the two books were all corrected, line by line commented, and former schools' old notes that truly developed subtle meaning were gathered for reference, as the head of the whole work marking the correct track.

sentences.zh: 次刪補名醫方論，次四診要訣，次諸病心法要訣，次正骨心法要旨。

translations.literal: Next deleting and supplementing famous physicians' formula treatises, next Essentials of the Four Examinations, next Essentials of Heart Methods for Various Diseases, next Essentials of Orthopedic Heart Methods.
translations.idiomatic: Next deleting and supplementing famous physicians' formula treatises, next Essentials of the Four Examinations, next Essentials of Heart Methods for Various Diseases, next Essentials of Orthopedic Heart Methods.

sentences.zh: 書成，賜名醫宗金鑑，雖出眾手編輯，而訂正傷寒、金匱，本于謙所自撰。

translations.literal: When complete it was named Golden Mirror of the Medical Tradition; though compiled by many hands, correcting Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer was based on Qian's own writing.
translations.idiomatic: When complete it was named Golden Mirror of the Medical Tradition. Though compiled by many hands, correcting Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer was based on Qian's own writing.

sentences.zh: 其採引清代乾​​隆以前醫說凡二十餘家，張璐、喻昌、徐彬、張志聰、高世式、張錫駒、柯琴、尤怡，事具本傳。

translations.literal: It cites more than twenty Qing medical sayings before Qianlong: Zhang Lu, Yu Chang, Xu Bin, Zhang Zhicong, Gao Shizong, Zhang Xiju, Ke Qin, You Yi—all in their main biographies.
translations.idiomatic: It cites more than twenty Qing medical sayings before Qianlong: Zhang Lu, Yu Chang, Xu Bin, Zhang Zhicong, Gao Shizong, Zhang Xiju, Ke Qin, You Yi—all in their main biographies.

sentences.zh: 其次者：林瀾，著傷寒折衷、靈素合鈔，兼通星象、堪輿之學；

translations.literal: Next in rank: Lin Lan, wrote Cold Damage Reconciliation and Combined Jade of Lingshu and Suwen, also penetrating astronomy and geomancy;
translations.idiomatic: Next in rank: Lin Lan wrote Cold Damage Reconciliation and Combined Jade of Lingshu and Suwen, also penetrating astronomy and geomancy;

sentences.zh: 汪琥，著傷寒論辨注；

translations.literal: Wang Hu, wrote Commentary and Discrimination on Cold Damage;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hu wrote Commentary and Discrimination on Cold Damage;

sentences.zh: 魏荔彤，著傷寒金匱本義；

translations.literal: Wei Lizhi, wrote Root Meaning of Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer;
translations.idiomatic: Wei Lizhi wrote Root Meaning of Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer;

sentences.zh: 沈明宗，著傷寒金匱編註；

translations.literal: Shen Mingzong, wrote Compiled Commentary on Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer;
translations.idiomatic: Shen Mingzong wrote Compiled Commentary on Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer;

sentences.zh: 程應旄，著傷寒後條辨；

translations.literal: Cheng Yingmao, wrote Later Detailed Differentiation of Cold Damage;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yingmao wrote Later Detailed Differentiation of Cold Damage;

sentences.zh: 鄭重光，著傷寒論條辨續注；

translations.literal: Zheng Chongguang, wrote Continued Commentary on Detailed Differentiation of Cold Damage;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chongguang wrote Continued Commentary on Detailed Differentiation of Cold Damage;

sentences.zh: 周揚俊，著傷寒三注、金匱二注；

translations.literal: Zhou Yangjun, wrote Three Commentaries on Cold Damage and Two on the Golden Coffer;
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yangjun wrote Three Commentaries on Cold Damage and Two on the Golden Coffer;

sentences.zh: 程林，著金匱直解、聖濟總錄纂要；

translations.literal: Cheng Lin, wrote Straight Explanation of the Golden Coffer and Essentials of the Sagely Relief General Collection;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lin wrote Straight Explanation of the Golden Coffer and Essentials of the Sagely Relief General Collection;

sentences.zh: 閔芝慶，著傷寒闡要編。

translations.literal: Min Zhiqing, wrote Compiled Essentials of Cold Damage.
translations.idiomatic: Min Zhiqing wrote Compiled Essentials of Cold Damage.

sentences.zh: 而遺書湮沒無考者，尚六七家云。

translations.literal: Yet lost books beyond inquiry number six or seven more.
translations.idiomatic: Yet lost books beyond inquiry number six or seven more.

sentences.zh: 綽爾濟，墨爾根氏，蒙古人。

translations.literal: Chuoerji, of the Moergen clan, a Mongol.
translations.idiomatic: Chuoerji, of the Moergen clan, was a Mongol.

sentences.zh: 天命中，率先歸附。

translations.literal: In the Tianming reign he was first to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianming reign he was first to submit.

sentences.zh: 善醫傷。

translations.literal: Skilled in treating wounds.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in treating wounds.

sentences.zh: 時白旗先鋒鄂碩與敵戰，中矢垂斃，綽爾濟為拔鏃，傅良藥，傷尋愈。

translations.literal: When White Banner vanguard Eshuo fought the enemy and was struck by an arrow near death, Chuoerji pulled the shaft, applied good medicine, and the wound soon healed.
translations.idiomatic: When White Banner vanguard Eshuo fought the enemy and was struck by an arrow near death, Chuoerji pulled the shaft, applied good medicine, and the wound soon healed.

sentences.zh: 都統武拜身被三十餘矢，昏絕，綽爾濟令剖白駝腹，置武拜其中，遂甦。

translations.literal: Commander Wubai was struck by more than thirty arrows and fainted; Chuoerji had a white camel's belly cut open and placed Wubai within, and he revived.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Wubai was struck by more than thirty arrows and fainted. Chuoerji had a white camel's belly cut open and placed Wubai within, and he revived.

sentences.zh: 有患臂屈不伸者，令先以熱鑊熏蒸，然後斧椎其骨，揉之有聲，即愈。

translations.literal: One whose arm would not straighten was first steamed with a hot pot, then the bone was chopped with axe and mallet; when rubbing made a sound, he immediately recovered.
translations.idiomatic: One whose arm would not straighten was first steamed with a hot pot, then the bone was chopped with axe and mallet. When rubbing made a sound, he immediately recovered.

sentences.zh: 覺羅伊桑阿，乾隆中，以正骨起家，至鉅富。

translations.literal: Yisang'a of the Aisin Gioro clan in the Qianlong reign rose from bone-setting to great wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Yisang'a of the Aisin Gioro clan in the Qianlong reign rose from bone-setting to great wealth.

sentences.zh: 其授徒法，削筆管為數段，包以紙，摩挲之，使其節節皆接合，如未斷者然，乃如法接骨，皆奏效。

translations.literal: His method of teaching disciples: cut a pen tube into sections, wrap with paper and rub until each joint joins as if unbroken—then set bones by the method and all succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His method of teaching disciples: cut a pen tube into sections, wrap with paper and rub until each joint joins as if unbroken—then set bones by the method and all succeeded.

sentences.zh: 故事，選上三旗士卒之明骨法者，每旗十人，隸上駟院，名蒙古醫士。

translations.literal: By precedent, from the Upper Three Banners ten men per banner skilled in bone method were chosen for the Imperial Stud, called Mongol physicians.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, from the Upper Three Banners ten men per banner skilled in bone method were chosen for the Imperial Stud, called Mongol physicians.

sentences.zh: 凡禁庭執事人有跌損者，命醫治，限日報痊，逾期則懲治之。

translations.literal: Whenever palace attendants suffered falls, physicians were ordered to treat and report recovery by a deadline; overdue brought punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever palace attendants suffered falls, physicians were ordered to treat and report recovery by a deadline; overdue brought punishment.

sentences.zh: 侍郎齊召南墜馬，傷首，腦出。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Qi Zhaonan fell from a horse, injuring his head; brain protruded.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Qi Zhaonan fell from a horse, injuring his head, and his brain protruded.

sentences.zh: 蒙古醫士以牛脬蒙其首，其創立愈。

translations.literal: The Mongol physician covered his head with an ox bladder and the wound soon healed.
translations.idiomatic: The Mongol physician covered his head with an ox bladder and the wound soon healed.

sentences.zh: 時有秘方，能立奏效，伊桑阿名最著。

translations.literal: At the time there were secret formulas with immediate effect; Yisang'a's name was most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were secret formulas with immediate effect; Yisang'a's name was most renowned.

sentences.zh: 當時湖南有張朝魁者，亦以治傷科聞。

translations.literal: At the time in Hunan Zhang Chaokui was also famed for trauma medicine.
translations.idiomatic: At the time in Hunan Zhang Chaokui was also famed for trauma medicine.

sentences.zh: 朝魁，辰谿人，又名毛矮子。

translations.literal: Chaokui, a man of Chenxi, also called Shorty Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Chaokui, a man of Chenxi, was also called Shorty Mao.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，遇遠來乞者，朝魁厚待之，乞者授以異術，治癰疽、瘰癧及跌打、損傷、危急之證，能以刀剖皮肉，去淤血於臟腑。

translations.literal: At twenty-odd he met a distant beggar whom he treated generously; the beggar taught him occult arts for abscess, scrofula, falls, injuries, and critical cases—able to cut flesh with a knife and remove stagnant blood from viscera.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-odd he met a distant beggar whom he treated generously. The beggar taught him occult arts for abscess, scrofula, falls, injuries, and critical cases—able to cut flesh with a knife and remove stagnant blood from viscera.

sentences.zh: 又能續筋正骨，時有劉某患腹痛，僕地瀕死，朝魁往視曰：「病在大小腸。」

translations.literal: He could also join sinews and set bones. Once Liu suffered abdominal pain, fell prostrate near death; Chaokui went and said: "The disease is in the large and small intestine."
translations.idiomatic: He could also join sinews and set bones. Once Liu suffered abdominal pain and fell prostrate near death. Chaokui went and said: "The disease is in the large and small intestine."

sentences.zh: 剖其腹二寸許，伸指入腹理之，數日愈。

translations.literal: He cut the belly two cun and reached in with a finger to arrange the intestines; in days he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He cut the belly two cun and reached in with a finger to arrange the intestines; in days he recovered.

sentences.zh: 辰州知府某乘輿越銀壺山，忽墮岩下，折髃骨，朝魁以刀刺之，撥正，傅以藥，運動如常。

translations.literal: A prefect crossed Silver Pot Mountain in a sedan, suddenly fell from a cliff and broke the hip bone; Chaokui pierced with a knife, set it right, applied medicine, and movement was normal.
translations.idiomatic: A prefect crossed Silver Pot Mountain in a sedan, suddenly fell from a cliff and broke the hip bone. Chaokui pierced with a knife, set it right, applied medicine, and movement was normal.

sentences.zh: 陸懋修，字九芝，江蘇元和人。

translations.literal: Lu Maoxiu, courtesy name Jiuzhi, a native of Yuanhe in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Maoxiu, courtesy name Jiuzhi, was a native of Yuanhe in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 先世以儒顯，皆通醫。

translations.literal: His forebears were eminent in Confucian learning, all penetrating medicine.
translations.idiomatic: His forebears were eminent in Confucian learning and all penetrated medicine.

sentences.zh: 懋修為諸生，世其學。

translations.literal: Maoxiu was a licentiate and inherited the profession.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxiu was a licentiate and inherited the profession.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，粵匪擾江南，轉徙上海，遂以醫名。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng reign the Taiping rebels disturbed Jiangnan; he moved to Shanghai and became famed in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng reign the Taiping rebels disturbed Jiangnan. He moved to Shanghai and became famed in medicine.

sentences.zh: 研精素問，著內經運氣病釋。

translations.literal: He studied Suwen deeply and wrote Explanation of Disease from Celestial Motion and Qi in the Inner Canon.
translations.idiomatic: He studied Suwen deeply and wrote Explanation of Disease from Celestial Motion and Qi in the Inner Canon.

sentences.zh: 後益博通漢以後書，恪守仲景家法，於有清一代醫家，悉舉其得失。

translations.literal: Later he broadly penetrated books from Han onward, kept to Zhongjing's family method, and for Qing physicians entirely raised their gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: Later he broadly penetrated books from Han onward, kept to Zhongjing's family method, and for Qing physicians entirely raised their gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 所取法在柯琴、尤怡兩家，謂得仲景意較多。

translations.literal: His models were Ke Qin and You Yi, said to obtain Zhongjing's meaning more.
translations.idiomatic: His models were Ke Qin and You Yi, said to obtain Zhongjing's meaning more fully.

sentences.zh: 吳中葉桂名最盛，傳最廣，懋修謂桂醫案出門弟子，不盡可信。

translations.literal: Ye Gui of Wu was most famed and most widely transmitted; Maoxiu said Gui's medical cases came from door disciples and are not fully trustworthy.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Gui of Wu was most famed and most widely transmitted. Maoxiu said Gui's medical cases came from door disciples and are not fully trustworthy.

sentences.zh: 所傳溫病證治，亦門人筆述。

translations.literal: The transmitted warm disease pattern treatment is also disciples' brush notes.
translations.idiomatic: The transmitted warm disease pattern treatment is also disciples' brush notes.

sentences.zh: 開卷揭「溫邪上受、首先犯肺、逆傳心包」一語，不應經法，誤以胃熱為肺熱，由於不識陽明病，故著陽明病釋一篇，以闡明之。

translations.literal: Opening with "warm evil ascends and first invades the lung, reversely transmitting to the pericardium" does not accord with classic method, mistaking stomach heat for lung heat from not knowing yangming disease; therefore he wrote one treatise Explaining Yangming Disease to clarify.
translations.idiomatic: Opening with "warm evil ascends and first invades the lung, reversely transmitting to the pericardium" does not accord with classic method, mistaking stomach heat for lung heat from not knowing yangming disease. Therefore he wrote Explaining Yangming Disease to clarify.

sentences.zh: 又據難經「傷寒有五」之文，謂：「仲景撰用難經，溫病即在傷寒中，治溫病法不出傷寒論外。」

translations.literal: Also according to the Difficult Classic "cold damage has five kinds," he said: "Zhongjing adopted the Difficult Classic; warm disease is within cold damage, and methods for warm disease do not go outside Cold Damage."
translations.idiomatic: Also according to the Difficult Classic "cold damage has five kinds," he said: "Zhongjing adopted the Difficult Classic. Warm disease is within cold damage, and methods for warm disease do not go outside Cold Damage."

sentences.zh: 又謂：「瘟疫有溫、有寒，與溫病不同，醫者多混稱。

translations.literal: He also said: "Pestilence has warm and cold, different from warm disease; physicians often confuse the names.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Pestilence has warm and cold, different from warm disease; physicians often confuse the names.

sentences.zh: 吳有性、戴天章為治疫專家，且不免此誤。」

translations.literal: Wu Youxing and Dai Tianzhang as pestilence specialists still did not avoid this error."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Youxing and Dai Tianzhang as pestilence specialists still did not avoid this error."

sentences.zh: 著論辨之，並精確，有功學者。

translations.literal: He wrote treatises to discriminate, all precise, with merit for students.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote treatises to discriminate, all precise, with merit for students.

sentences.zh: 懋修既棄舉業，不求仕進，及子潤庠登第，就養京邸，著述至老不倦。

translations.literal: Maoxiu abandoned the examination career and did not seek advancement; when his son Runku became a provincial graduate he nourished him in the capital and wrote to old age without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxiu abandoned the examination career and did not seek advancement. When his son Runku became a provincial graduate he nourished him in the capital and wrote to old age without weariness.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，卒。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu reign he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu reign he died.

sentences.zh: 潤庠亦通醫，官至大學士，自有傳。

translations.literal: Runku also penetrated medicine, rose to Grand Secretary, and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Runku also penetrated medicine, rose to Grand Secretary, and has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 王丙，字樸莊，吳縣人，懋修之外曾祖也。

translations.literal: Wang Bing, courtesy name Puzhuang, a man of Wu County, Maoxiu's great-grandfather on the mother's side.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bing, courtesy name Puzhuang, was a man of Wu County and Maoxiu's great-grandfather on the mother's side.

sentences.zh: 著傷寒論注，以唐孫思邈千金方僅採王叔和傷寒論序例，全書載翼方中，序次最古，據為定本。

translations.literal: He wrote Commentary on Cold Damage, taking Tang Sun Simiao's Thousand Gold Formulas which only adopted Wang Shuhe's Cold Damage preface and arrangement—the whole book loads wing formulas, the oldest order—and took it as the fixed edition.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Commentary on Cold Damage, taking Tang Sun Simiao's Thousand Gold Formulas which only adopted Wang Shuhe's Cold Damage preface and arrangement—the whole book loads wing formulas in the oldest order—and took it as the fixed edition.

sentences.zh: 謂：「方中行、喻昌等刪駁序例，乃欲申己見，非定論。」

translations.literal: He said: "Fang Zhongxing, Yu Chang, and others deleted and refuted the preface and arrangement to extend their own views—not fixed conclusion."
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Fang Zhongxing, Yu Chang, and others deleted and refuted the preface and arrangement to extend their own views—not fixed conclusion."

sentences.zh: 著迴瀾說，爭之甚力。

translations.literal: He wrote Returning Tides Discourse, arguing very forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Returning Tides Discourse, arguing very forcefully.

sentences.zh: 又著古今權量考，古一兩準今六分七釐，一升準今七勺七秒，承學者奉以為法。

translations.literal: Also wrote Ancient and Modern Weights and Measures Examined: one ancient liang equals today six fen seven li; one sheng equals today seven spoon seven second—students took it as law.
translations.idiomatic: Also wrote Ancient and Modern Weights and Measures Examined: one ancient liang equals today six fen seven li; one sheng equals today seven spoon seven second—students took it as law.

sentences.zh: 呂震，字茶村，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Lü Zhen, courtesy name Chacun, a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen, courtesy name Chacun, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光五年舉人，官湖北荊門州判。

translations.literal: Provincial graduate in the fifth year of Daoguang, served as assistant magistrate of Jingmen in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was a provincial graduate in the fifth year of Daoguang and served as assistant magistrate of Jingmen in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 晚寓吳，酷嗜醫，診療輒有奇效。

translations.literal: In old age he lived in Wu, passionately fond of medicine; diagnosis and treatment often had remarkable effect.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he lived in Wu, passionately fond of medicine; diagnosis and treatment often had remarkable effect.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「傷寒論使學者有切實下手工夫，不止為傷寒立法。

translations.literal: He said: "Cold Damage lets students have real practical effort, not only legislating for cold damage.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Cold Damage lets students have real practical effort, not only legislating for cold damage.

sentences.zh: 能從六經辨證，雖繁劇如傷寒，不為多歧所誤，雜證一以貫之。」

translations.literal: One can discriminate patterns from the six channels; though as complex as cold damage one is not misled by many divergences, and miscellaneous patterns are threaded on one string."
translations.idiomatic: One can discriminate patterns from the six channels. Though as complex as cold damage, one is not misled by many divergences, and miscellaneous patterns are threaded on one string."

sentences.zh: 著內經要論、傷寒尋源。

translations.literal: He wrote Essentials of the Inner Canon and Seeking the Source of Cold Damage.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essentials of the Inner Canon and Seeking the Source of Cold Damage.

sentences.zh: 懋修持論多本丙、震云。

translations.literal: Maoxiu's holding to doctrine mostly derives from Bing and Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Maoxiu's holding to doctrine mostly derives from Bing and Zhen.

sentences.zh: 鄒澍，字潤安，江蘇武進人。

translations.literal: Zou Shu, courtesy name Run'an, a native of Wujin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Shu, courtesy name Run'an, was a native of Wujin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 有孝行，家貧績學，隱於醫。

translations.literal: Filial in conduct, poor in family but diligent in learning, he hid in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Filial in conduct, poor in family but diligent in learning, he hid in medicine.

sentences.zh: 道光初，詔舉山林隱逸，鄉人議以澍名上，固辭。

translations.literal: In early Daoguang an edict nominated recluses in mountains and forests; fellow townsmen proposed Shu's name but he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In early Daoguang an edict nominated recluses in mountains and forests. Fellow townsmen proposed Shu's name but he firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 澍通知天文推步、地理形勢沿革，詩古文亦卓然成家，不自表襮。

translations.literal: Shu knew astronomy, calendrical calculation, and geographical changes; poetry and ancient prose also established a school, yet he did not display himself.
translations.idiomatic: Shu knew astronomy, calendrical calculation, and geographical changes. His poetry and ancient prose also established a school, yet he did not display himself.

sentences.zh: 所著書，醫家言為多。

translations.literal: His writings are mostly medical.
translations.idiomatic: His writings are mostly medical.

sentences.zh: 傷寒通解、傷寒金匱方解、醫理摘要、醫經書目，並不傳。

translations.literal: General Explanation of Cold Damage, Formula Explanation of Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer, Medical Summary, and Medical Canon Bibliography—all do not circulate.
translations.idiomatic: General Explanation of Cold Damage, Formula Explanation of Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer, Medical Summary, and Medical Canon Bibliography—all do not circulate.

sentences.zh: 所刊行者，本經疏證、續疏證、本經序疏要。

translations.literal: What was printed: Commentary on the Root Classic, Continued Commentary, and Essentials of Preface and Commentary on the Root Classic.
translations.idiomatic: What was printed: Commentary on the Root Classic, Continued Commentary, and Essentials of Preface and Commentary on the Root Classic.

sentences.zh: 謂明潛江劉氏本草述，貫串金、元諸家說，反多牽掣，故所注悉本傷寒、金匱，疏通證明，而以千金、外台副之。

translations.literal: He said Ming Qianjiang Liu's Materia Medica Narrative strung together Jin and Yuan schools but had many constraints; therefore his notes all derive from Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer, clarifying proof, with Thousand Gold and Outer Terrace as supplement.
translations.idiomatic: He said Ming Qianjiang Liu's Materia Medica Narrative strung together Jin and Yuan schools but had many constraints. Therefore his notes all derive from Cold Damage and the Golden Coffer, clarifying proof, with Thousand Gold and Outer Terrace as supplement.

sentences.zh: 深究仲景制方精意，成一家之言。

translations.literal: He deeply investigated Zhongjing's formula intent and formed a school of his own.
translations.idiomatic: He deeply investigated Zhongjing's formula intent and formed a school of his own.

sentences.zh: 費伯雄，字晉卿。

translations.literal: Fei Boxiong, courtesy name Jinqing.
translations.idiomatic: Fei Boxiong, courtesy name Jinqing.

sentences.zh: 與澍同邑，居孟河，濱江。

translations.literal: Of the same district as Shu, he lived at Menghe on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Of the same district as Shu, he lived at Menghe on the river.

sentences.zh: 咸、同間以醫名遠近，詣診者踵相接，所居遂成繁盛之區。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns his medical name reached far and near; those seeking diagnosis came in succession, and his dwelling became a flourishing district.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianfeng and Tongzhi reigns his medical name reached far and near. Those seeking diagnosis came in succession, and his dwelling became a flourishing district.

sentences.zh: 持脈知病，不待問。

translations.literal: Taking the pulse he knew the disease without waiting to ask.
translations.idiomatic: Taking the pulse he knew the disease without waiting to ask.

sentences.zh: 論醫，戒偏戒雜。

translations.literal: In discussing medicine he warned against partiality and confusion.
translations.idiomatic: In discussing medicine he warned against partiality and confusion.

sentences.zh: 謂古醫以「和緩」命名，可通其意。

translations.literal: He said ancient physicians took "harmony and ease" as their name, which can communicate the meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He said ancient physicians took "harmony and ease" as their name, which can communicate the meaning.

sentences.zh: 著書曰醫醇，毀於寇。

translations.literal: His book was called Medical Essence, destroyed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: His book was called Medical Essence, destroyed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 撮其要，成醫醇賸義，附方論。

translations.literal: He extracted the essentials into Remaining Meaning of Medical Essence, with appended formula treatises.
translations.idiomatic: He extracted the essentials into Remaining Meaning of Medical Essence, with appended formula treatises.

sentences.zh: 大旨謂常病多，奇病少，醫者執簡，始能馭繁，不可尚異。

translations.literal: The main idea is that common diseases are many and strange diseases few; physicians who hold to simplicity can govern complexity and must not esteem the unusual.
translations.idiomatic: The main idea is that common diseases are many and strange diseases few. Physicians who hold to simplicity can govern complexity and must not esteem the unusual.

sentences.zh: 享盛名數十年，家以致富，子孫皆世其業。

translations.literal: He enjoyed great fame for decades; the family grew rich and descendants all inherited the profession.
translations.idiomatic: He enjoyed great fame for decades. The family grew rich and descendants all inherited the profession.

sentences.zh: 伯雄所著，詳於雜病，略於傷寒，與懋修、澍宗旨並不同。

translations.literal: Boxiong's writings are detailed on miscellaneous disease, brief on cold damage—aims different from Maoxiu and Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiong's writings are detailed on miscellaneous disease and brief on cold damage—aims different from Maoxiu and Shu.

sentences.zh: 清末江南諸醫，以伯雄為最著，用附載焉。

translations.literal: Among late Qing physicians of Jiangnan, Boxiong was most renowned and is appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Among late Qing physicians of Jiangnan, Boxiong was most renowned and is appended here.

sentences.zh: 清代醫學，多重考古，當道光中，始譯泰西醫書，王清任著醫林改錯。

translations.literal: Qing medicine mostly valued antiquarian study; in the Daoguang reign Western medical books began to be translated; Wang Qingren wrote Correcting Errors in the Medical Forest.
translations.idiomatic: Qing medicine mostly valued antiquarian study. In the Daoguang reign Western medical books began to be translated, and Wang Qingren wrote Correcting Errors in the Medical Forest.

sentences.zh: 以中國無解剖之學，宋、元後相傳臟腑諸圖，疑不盡合，於刑人時，考驗有得，參證獸畜。

translations.literal: China had no anatomy; viscera diagrams transmitted from Song and Yuan he doubted were not fully correct; at executions he examined and compared with domestic animals.
translations.idiomatic: China had no anatomy. Viscera diagrams transmitted from Song and Yuan he doubted were not fully correct. At executions he examined and compared with domestic animals.

sentences.zh: 未見西書，而其說與合。

translations.literal: He had not seen Western books, yet his sayings accorded.
translations.idiomatic: He had not seen Western books, yet his sayings accorded with them.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，唐宗海推廣其義，證以內經異同，經脈奇經各穴，及營衛經氣，為西醫所未及。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu reign Tang Zonghai extended the meaning, comparing with Inner Canon differences, extraordinary channels and points, and nutritive-defensive channel qi—what Western medicine had not reached.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guangxu reign Tang Zonghai extended the meaning, comparing with Inner Canon differences, extraordinary channels and points, and nutritive-defensive channel qi—what Western medicine had not reached.

sentences.zh: 著中西匯通醫經精義，欲通其郵而補其缺。

translations.literal: He wrote Essential Meaning of Chinese and Western Combined Medical Canon, wishing to connect the posts and fill the gaps.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote Essential Meaning of Chinese and Western Combined Medical Canon, wishing to connect the posts and fill the gaps.

sentences.zh: 兩人之開悟，皆足以啟後者。

translations.literal: Both men's enlightenment suffices to inspire those after.
translations.idiomatic: Both men's enlightenment suffices to inspire those after.

sentences.zh: 蔣平階，字大鴻，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: Jiang Pingjie, courtesy name Dahong, a native of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Pingjie, courtesy name Dahong, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，其祖命習形家之學，十年，始得其傳。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, his grandfather ordered him to study form-school learning; ten years before he obtained the transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, his grandfather ordered him to study form-school learning. Ten years passed before he obtained the transmission.

sentences.zh: 遍證之大江南、北古今名墓，又十年，始得其旨；

translations.literal: He verified great and small, ancient and modern famous tombs north and south of the great rivers; another ten years before he obtained the aim;
translations.idiomatic: He verified great and small, ancient and modern famous tombs north and south of the great rivers. Another ten years passed before he obtained the aim;

sentences.zh: 又十年，始窮其變。

translations.literal: another ten years before he exhausted the changes.
translations.idiomatic: another ten years before he exhausted the changes.

sentences.zh: 自謂視天下山川土壤，雖大荒內外如一也。

translations.literal: He said he viewed all mountains, rivers, and soil under heaven, even within the great wilds, as one.
translations.idiomatic: He said he viewed all mountains, rivers, and soil under heaven, even within the great wilds, as one.

sentences.zh: 遂著地理辨正，取當世相傳之書，訂其紕繆，析其是非，惟尊唐楊筠鬆一人，曾文辿僅因筠松以傳。

translations.literal: He then wrote Discriminating Geography, taking books transmitted in the age, correcting errors, analyzing right and wrong, revering only Tang Yang Junsong; Zeng Wenchuan transmitted only through Junsong.
translations.idiomatic: He then wrote Discriminating Geography, taking books transmitted in the age, correcting errors and analyzing right and wrong, revering only Tang Yang Junsong. Zeng Wenchuan transmitted only through Junsong.

sentences.zh: 其於廖瑀、賴文俊、何溥以下，視之蔑如。

translations.literal: Of Liao Yu, Lai Wenjun, He Pu and below he regarded them as nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Of Liao Yu, Lai Wenjun, He Pu and below he regarded them as nothing.

sentences.zh: 以世所惑溺者，莫甚於平砂玉尺一書，斥其偽尤力。

translations.literal: What the world is most deluded by is none more than Level Sand Jade Ruler; he rebuked its falsity especially forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: What the world is most deluded by is none more than Level Sand Jade Ruler. He rebuked its falsity especially forcefully.

sentences.zh: 自言事貴心授，非可言罄，古書充棟，半屬偽造。

translations.literal: He said the matter values heart transmission and cannot be fully spoken; ancient books fill rafters, half forged.
translations.idiomatic: He said the matter values heart transmission and cannot be fully spoken. Ancient books fill the rafters, half of them forged.

sentences.zh: 其昌言救世，惟在地理辨正一書。

translations.literal: His loud voice to save the age rests only in Discriminating Geography.
translations.idiomatic: His loud voice to save the age rests only in Discriminating Geography.

sentences.zh: 後復自抒所得，作天元五歌，謂此皆糟粕，其精微亦不在此，他無秘本。

translations.literal: Later he expressed his own attainments in Five Songs of Celestial Origin, saying these are all dregs and the subtle is not in them; he had no other secret editions.
translations.idiomatic: Later he expressed his own attainments in Five Songs of Celestial Origin, saying these are all dregs and the subtle is not in them. He had no other secret editions.

sentences.zh: 三吳兩浙，有自稱得平階真傳及偽撰成書指為平階秘本者，皆假託也。

translations.literal: In the three Wu and two Zhe regions some claimed Pingjie's true transmission or forged books as Pingjie secret editions—all false.
translations.idiomatic: In the three Wu and two Zhe regions some claimed Pingjie's true transmission or forged books as Pingjie secret editions—all false.

sentences.zh: 從之學者，丹陽張仲馨，丹徒駱士鵬，山陰呂相烈，會稽姜堯，武陵胡泰徵，淄川畢世持，他無所傳授。

translations.literal: Students: Danyang Zhang Zhongxin, Dantu Luo Shipeng, Shanyin Lü Xianglie, Kuaiji Jiang Yao, Wuling Hu Taiwei, Zichuan Bi Shichi—no other transmission.
translations.idiomatic: His students were Danyang Zhang Zhongxin, Dantu Luo Shipeng, Shanyin Lü Xianglie, Kuaiji Jiang Yao, Wuling Hu Taiwei, and Zichuan Bi Shichi—no other transmission.

sentences.zh: 姜堯注青囊奧語及平砂玉尺辨偽，總括歌，即附地理辨正中。

translations.literal: Jiang Yao commented on Green Bag Secret Language and forged Level Sand Jade Ruler, summary songs—all appended in Discriminating Geography.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yao commented on Green Bag Secret Language and forged Level Sand Jade Ruler summary songs—all appended in Discriminating Geography.

sentences.zh: 平階生於明末，兼以詩鳴。

translations.literal: Pingjie was born in the late Ming and was also famed in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Pingjie was born in the late Ming and was also famed in poetry.

sentences.zh: 清初諸老，多與唱和。

translations.literal: Early Qing elders mostly exchanged poems with him.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qing elders mostly exchanged poems with him.

sentences.zh: 地學為一代大宗，所造羅經，後人多用之，稱為「蔣盤」雲。

translations.literal: In geomancy he was a great master of the age; the compass he made later men mostly used, called the "Jiang Plate."
translations.idiomatic: In geomancy he was a great master of the age. The compass he made later men mostly used, called the "Jiang Plate."

sentences.zh: 章攀桂，字淮樹，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Pangui, courtesy name Huaishu, a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pangui, courtesy name Huaishu, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，官甘肅知縣，累擢江蘇松太兵備道。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong reign he served as magistrate in Gansu, rose to Jiangsu Song-Tai circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong reign he served as magistrate in Gansu and rose to Jiangsu Song-Tai circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 有吏才，多術藝，尤精形家言。

translations.literal: He had administrative talent and many arts, especially penetrating form-school doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: He had administrative talent and many arts, especially penetrating form-school doctrine.

sentences.zh: 謂近世形家諸書，理當辭顯者，莫如明張宗道地理全書，為之作注，稍辨正其誤失。

translations.literal: He said among recent form-school books, for clear principle none surpasses Ming Zhang Zongdao's Complete Geography; he made commentary, slightly correcting errors.
translations.idiomatic: He said among recent form-school books, for clear principle none surpasses Ming Zhang Zongdao's Complete Geography. He made commentary, slightly correcting errors.

sentences.zh: 大旨本元人山陽指迷之說，專主形勢。

translations.literal: The main idea derives from Yuan Shan Yang Pointing the Way, chiefly terrain.
translations.idiomatic: The main idea derives from Yuan Shan Yang Pointing the Way, chiefly terrain.

sentences.zh: 攀桂既仕顯，不以方技為業，自喜其術，每為親族交友擇地，貧者助之財以葬。

translations.literal: Pangui having risen to prominence did not take technique as profession; he delighted in his art and often chose ground for kin and friends; for the poor he helped with burial funds.
translations.idiomatic: Though Pangui had risen to prominence, he did not take technique as his profession. He delighted in his art and often chose ground for kin and friends; for the poor he helped with burial funds.

sentences.zh: 妻吳故農家，自恨門第微，攀桂為購佳壤葬其親，擇子弟秀異者撫教之，遂登進士第，為望族。

translations.literal: His wife Wu was formerly a farming family; resenting humble station, Pangui bought fine ground to bury her kin, chose gifted youths to nurture, and they became jinshi—the family a leading clan.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Wu was formerly from a farming family. Resenting humble station, Pangui bought fine ground to bury her kin, chose gifted youths to nurture, and they became jinshi—the family a leading clan.

sentences.zh: 高宗數南巡，自鎮江至江寧，江行險，每由陸。

translations.literal: The Gaozong Emperor several times toured south; from Zhenjiang to Jiangning the river route was dangerous and he often went by land.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaozong Emperor several times toured south. From Zhenjiang to Jiangning the river route was dangerous and he often went by land.

sentences.zh: 詔改通水道，議鑿句容故破岡瀆，攀桂相其地勢，謂茅山石巨勢高，縱成瀆，非設閘不可成，儲水多勞費。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the water route improved; it was proposed to open the old Pogang canal at Jurong; Pangui surveyed terrain and said Maoshan stone was huge and high—even if a canal were made, sluices would be needed, storing much water at great cost.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the water route improved. It was proposed to open the old Pogang canal at Jurong. Pangui surveyed terrain and said Maoshan stone was huge and high—even if a canal were made, sluices would be needed, storing much water at great cost.

sentences.zh: 請從上元東北攝山下，鑿金烏珠刀槍河故道，以達丹徒，工省修​​易。

translations.literal: He requested from northeast Shangyuan below She Mountain to open the old Jindao He of the Golden Crow Pearl Knife Spear to reach Dantu—work saved and repair easy.
translations.idiomatic: He requested from northeast Shangyuan below She Mountain to open the old Jindao He of the Golden Crow Pearl Knife Spear to reach Dantu—work saved and repair easy.

sentences.zh: 遂監其役，瀆成，謂之新河，百年來賴其利便，攀桂亦因獲優擢。

translations.literal: He supervised the work; when the canal was complete it was called the New River; for a hundred years its convenience was relied on and Pangui was preferentially promoted.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised the work. When the canal was complete it was called the New River. For a hundred years its convenience was relied on and Pangui was preferentially promoted.

sentences.zh: 大學士於敏中於金壇裡第築園，攀桂為之相度營建，敏中歿後，事覺，高宗惡之，褫職居江寧。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yu Minzhong built a garden at his Jin Tan estate; Pangui surveyed and built it. After Minzhong died the matter came out; the emperor hated it and stripped his office; he lived in Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yu Minzhong built a garden at his Jin Tan estate. Pangui surveyed and built it. After Minzhong died the matter came out. The emperor hated it and stripped his office; he lived in Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 晚耽禪理，歿時預知期日。

translations.literal: In old age he devoted himself to Chan; at death he foreknew the day.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he devoted himself to Chan. At death he foreknew the day.

sentences.zh: 兼通日者術，括協紀辨方精要為一書，曰選擇正宗，行於世。

translations.literal: Also penetrating day-selection, he condensed Essentials of Harmonizing Records and Selecting Directions into one book, Orthodox Selection, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Also penetrating day-selection, he condensed Essentials of Harmonizing Records and Selecting Directions into one book, Orthodox Selection, circulating in the world.

sentences.zh: 劉祿，河南人。

translations.literal: Liu Lu, a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lu was a man of Henan.

sentences.zh: 善風角。

translations.literal: Skilled in wind-angle divination.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in wind-angle divination.

sentences.zh: 聖祖召直蒙養齋，欲授以官，屢辭。

translations.literal: The Kangxi Emperor summoned him to the Mengyangzhai and wished to grant office; he repeatedly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi Emperor summoned him to the Mengyangzhai and wished to grant office, but he repeatedly declined.

sentences.zh: 從上北征，會糧餉乏濟，命卜之，曰：「不出三日必至。」

translations.literal: Following the northern expedition, when grain and funds were scarce he was ordered to divine and said: "Within three days it must arrive."
translations.idiomatic: Following the northern expedition, when grain and funds were scarce he was ordered to divine and said: "Within three days it must arrive."

sentences.zh: 果如其言。

translations.literal: It was as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It was as he said.

sentences.zh: 後從幸熱河，一日，踉蹌至宮門，請上速徙高阜以避水厄。

translations.literal: Later following the emperor to Rehe, one day he staggered to the palace gate and asked the emperor to move quickly to high ground to avoid water calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Later following the emperor to Rehe, one day he staggered to the palace gate and asked the emperor to move quickly to high ground to avoid water calamity.

sentences.zh: 時方晴霽，夜山水漲發，果衝沒行宮。

translations.literal: The weather was clear; at night mountain floods rose and indeed washed away the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: The weather was clear, but at night mountain floods rose and indeed washed away the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 又善相人，謂張廷玉、史貽直皆異日太平宰相。

translations.literal: Also skilled in physiognomy, he said Zhang Tingyu and Shi Yizhi would both be peace-era grand councilors.
translations.idiomatic: Also skilled in physiognomy, he said Zhang Tingyu and Shi Yizhi would both be peace-era grand councilors.

sentences.zh: 六十一年冬，乞假歸，至十一月望日，忽命家人制縗服，北向哭，未幾，哀詔至，正聖祖崩之後二日也。

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year winter he begged leave to return; on the fifteenth of the eleventh month he suddenly ordered the family to make mourning garments, cried northward, and soon the mourning edict arrived—exactly two days after the Kangxi Emperor's death.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixty-first year winter he begged leave to return. On the fifteenth of the eleventh month he suddenly ordered the family to make mourning garments, cried northward, and soon the mourning edict arrived—exactly two days after the Kangxi Emperor's death.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: Later he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died at home.

sentences.zh: 張永祚，字景韶，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yongzuo, courtesy name Jingshao, a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yongzuo, courtesy name Jingshao, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 幼即喜仰觀五緯，長通曉星學，究悉天象。

translations.literal: From youth he delighted in observing the five luminaries; grown, he thoroughly understood star learning and fully knew celestial phenomena.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he delighted in observing the five luminaries. Grown, he thoroughly understood star learning and fully knew celestial phenomena.

sentences.zh: 年近三十，督學王蘭生稔其學，錄為諸生。

translations.literal: Near thirty, Educational Commissioner Wang Lansheng knew his learning and enrolled him as licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: Near thirty, Educational Commissioner Wang Lansheng knew his learning and enrolled him as licentiate.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督嵇曾筠求通知星象者，試永祚策，立成數千言。

translations.literal: Fujian-Zhejiang Governor Ji Zengjun sought one knowing celestial phenomena; Yongzuo's examination answer was several thousand words at once.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian-Zhejiang Governor Ji Zengjun sought one knowing celestial phenomena. Yongzuo's examination answer was several thousand words at once.

sentences.zh: 薦於朝，授欽天監博士。

translations.literal: Recommended to court, he was appointed Astronomy Bureau doctor.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended to court, he was appointed Astronomy Bureau doctor.

sentences.zh: 屢引見，佔候悉驗。

translations.literal: Repeatedly summoned, his prognostications all verified.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly summoned, his prognostications all verified.

sentences.zh: 詔刊二十二史，永祚校勘天文、律曆兩志。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Twenty-two Histories printed; Yongzuo collated the astronomy and calendar treatises.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Twenty-two Histories printed. Yongzuo collated the astronomy and calendar treatises.

sentences.zh: 及書成，告歸。

translations.literal: When the book was complete he asked to return.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was complete he asked to return.

sentences.zh: 晚著書，曰天象原委。

translations.literal: In old age he wrote Origins of Celestial Phenomena.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he wrote Origins of Celestial Phenomena.

sentences.zh: 卒後，有女傳其學。

translations.literal: After death a daughter transmitted the learning.
translations.idiomatic: After death a daughter transmitted the learning.

sentences.zh: 壻沈度，亦善推步，守其書。

translations.literal: Son-in-law Shen Du also was skilled in calculation and kept his books.
translations.idiomatic: Son-in-law Shen Du was also skilled in calculation and kept his books.

sentences.zh: 戴尚文，湖南溆浦人。

translations.literal: Dai Shangwen, a native of Xupu in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Shangwen was a native of Xupu in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 從鴻臚卿羅典學，凡天官星卜諸書，無不究覽。

translations.literal: He studied with Grand Secretary Luo Dian; all books on celestial stars, divination, and numerology he investigated without exception.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with Grand Secretary Luo Dian. All books on celestial stars, divination, and numerology he investigated without exception.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾治經，師羅先生。

translations.literal: He once said: "I study the classics with Master Luo.
translations.idiomatic: He once said: "I study the classics with Master Luo.

sentences.zh: 吾術數，未知孰可吾師者？」

translations.literal: My numerology—I do not yet know who can be my teacher."
translations.idiomatic: My numerology—I do not yet know who can be my teacher."

sentences.zh: 聞江南某僧精六壬、奇門，往師焉，盡得其秘。

translations.literal: Hearing a Jiangnan monk skilled in liuren and qimen, he went as disciple and obtained all secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing a Jiangnan monk skilled in liuren and qimen, he went as disciple and obtained all secrets.

sentences.zh: 歸，應鄉試長沙，同舍生失金，尚文為占曰：「君金若干，盜者青衣，手魚肉，前行，後一白衣隨之，肩荷重物。

translations.literal: Returning, he took the provincial examination at Changsha; a roommate lost gold; Shangwen divined: "Your gold is so much; the thief wears blue, holds fish and meat, goes ahead, a white-clad follows shouldering heavy things.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, he took the provincial examination at Changsha. A roommate lost gold. Shangwen divined: "Your gold is so much. The thief wears blue, holds fish and meat, goes ahead, and a white-clad follows shouldering heavy things.

sentences.zh: 以某時，候驛步門外，可獲也。」

translations.literal: At such time wait outside Yibu Gate and you may capture him."
translations.idiomatic: At such time wait outside Yibu Gate and you may capture him."

sentences.zh: 如其言往，果驗。

translations.literal: Going as said, it verified.
translations.idiomatic: Going as said, it verified.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍母夜坐，心動，知偷兒入宅。

translations.literal: Once attending his mother at night he felt movement and knew a thief entered the house.
translations.idiomatic: Once attending his mother at night he felt movement and knew a thief had entered the house.

sentences.zh: 取井泥塗灶門，書符封之，偷不得去。

translations.literal: He took well mud to smear the stove door, wrote a talisman to seal it, and the thief could not leave.
translations.idiomatic: He took well mud to smear the stove door, wrote a talisman to seal it, and the thief could not leave.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶初，福康安徵苗，招致才異，羅典薦溆浦兩生，一嚴如煜，一即尚文。

translations.literal: In early Jiaqing Fukang'an campaigned against the Miao and gathered unusual talent; Luo Dian recommended two Xupu students—one Yan Ruyu, one Shangwen.
translations.idiomatic: In early Jiaqing Fukang'an campaigned against the Miao and gathered unusual talent. Luo Dian recommended two Xupu students—one Yan Ruyu, one Shangwen.

sentences.zh: 謂曰：「嚴生負經濟才，應祿仕；

translations.literal: He said: "Student Yan has economic talent and should receive office;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Student Yan has economic talent and should receive office;

sentences.zh: 汝疏散，為幕客，慎勿官職自羈也。」

translations.literal: you are scattered—be a staff adviser; carefully do not bind yourself with office."
translations.idiomatic: you are scattered—be a staff adviser; carefully do not bind yourself with office."

sentences.zh: 尚文見福康安，長揖不拜，福康安欲試其術，握絲帶問曰：「君神算，知吾握中何物？」

translations.literal: Shangwen met Fukang'an, bowed with clasped hands without kneeling; Fukang'an wished to test his art, grasped a silk belt and asked: "Sir divine calculation—know what I hold?"
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen met Fukang'an, bowed with clasped hands without kneeling. Fukang'an wished to test his art, grasped a silk belt and asked: "Sir divine calculation—know what I hold?"

sentences.zh: 乃請一字析其數，以五行推之，曰：「絲縷耳。」

translations.literal: He asked one character analyzed by number, deduced by five phases, and said: "Silk threads."
translations.idiomatic: He asked one character analyzed by number, deduced by five phases, and said: "Silk threads."

sentences.zh: 大驚異，禮遇之，凡事必諮。

translations.literal: Great astonishment; honored with courtesy; in all matters he was consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Great astonishment followed. Fukang'an honored him with courtesy and consulted him in all matters.

sentences.zh: 時苗猖獗，恆夜撲營，尚文輒預卜知之。

translations.literal: When the Miao were rampant, they constantly raided camps by night; Shangwen always foreknew by divination.
translations.idiomatic: When the Miao were rampant, they constantly raided camps by night, yet Shangwen always foreknew it by divination.

sentences.zh: 當五月，進攻旗鼓寨，佔：「有大雹，賊伏林莽，師出不利。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month, attacking Qigu Stockade, he divined: "Great hail will fall; the rebels hide in forest and scrub; the army's sortie is unfavorable."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, as they attacked Qigu Stockade, he divined and said: "Great hail will fall, the rebels hide in forest and scrub, and the army's sortie will be unfavorable."

sentences.zh: 勿聽。

translations.literal: They did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: They did not listen.

sentences.zh: 日午，將抵寨，忽大風，雷雨雹交下，如卵如拳，擊傷士卒，伏苗乘之，果敗。

translations.literal: At noon, about to reach the stockade, suddenly great wind; rain, thunder, and hail fell together, egg- and fist-sized, striking and wounding soldiers; Miao in ambush seized the moment and defeat followed.
translations.idiomatic: At noon, as they were about to reach the stockade, a great wind rose. Rain, thunder, and hail fell together, as large as eggs and fists, striking and wounding the soldiers. Miao in ambush seized the moment, and defeat followed.

sentences.zh: 軍中呼曰「神仙」。

translations.literal: The army called him "Immortal."
translations.idiomatic: The army called him "Immortal."

sentences.zh: 又大軍在乾州，營龍頭，為苗所圍，斷水，軍不得食。

translations.literal: Again the great army was at Qianzhou, encamped at Longtou, surrounded by Miao, water cut off, the army could not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Again the great army was at Qianzhou, encamped at Longtou, surrounded by the Miao with water cut off, so the army could not eat.

sentences.zh: 尚文設壇鑿池，以法禳之，劇地，清泉滃出。

translations.literal: Shangwen set up an altar and dug a pool, performed rites to avert calamity; in the fierce ground clear spring water gushed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen set up an altar and dug a pool, performed rites to avert the calamity, and from the hard ground clear spring water gushed forth.

sentences.zh: 四年，駐天心寨，尚文夜觀天象，知有咎，作書置幕府，辭歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, stationed at Tianxin Stockade, Shangwen observed the heavens at night, knew calamity was coming, left a letter at headquarters, and begged leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, while stationed at Tianxin Stockade, Shangwen observed the heavens at night, knew calamity was coming, left a letter at headquarters, and begged leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 數日，福康安遽卒。

translations.literal: Within days Fukang'an suddenly died.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Fukang'an died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 尚文歸未幾，亦病，自知死日。

translations.literal: Shangwen had not long returned when he too fell ill and knew the day of his death.
translations.idiomatic: Shangwen had not long returned when he too fell ill and knew the day he would die.

sentences.zh: 卒後，其母傷之，焚所傳書。

translations.literal: After death his mother grieved and burned the books he had transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his mother grieved for him and burned the books he had transmitted.
